arXiv:2607.27281v1 [cs.LG] 29 Jul 2026

The Kinetics of Training: A Driven-Nucleation Rate Law
for Emergence, Plasticity Loss, and Circuit Control in Language Models

Lei Dong Affiliation: Independent Researcher Email: dongleiit@hotmail.com
July 2026
Abstract

A capability appears in a language model when the last parts of its circuit align in one stochastic attempt, and getting all but one right is worth nothing. We show this no-partial-credit joint alignment is the rate-limiting step of capability formation. Two fingerprints: in a shortcut-free apparatus a five-part circuit missing three waits as long as a three-part circuit missing three (1.19–1.37), so the wait counts missing parts, not size; and on Pythia across seven capabilities and three scales, ablating one part leaves a median 17% of the capability in 32 of 32 discriminating cells, where partial credit predicts 50–83% (p=2×10−10p=2\times 10^{-10}), while a random non-part head leaves 100%.

One rare event whose barrier grows with missing parts yields one rate equation — sites ×\times attempts ×\times drive ×e−β​K\times\,e^{-\beta K}, minus destruction — read three ways, each preregistered with frozen constants. Forward: a capability flat at baseline ignites at a step of our choosing once the mix passes a concentration floor (10/10 above, 0/12 below), and while still flat its arrival is datable from its precursor to 5% median error on six held-out models. Backward: the delay to learn a withheld capability grows with waiting until, past a critical step, it never ignites — yet validation loss falls smoothly throughout, so standard monitors are blind to it. We locate the damage (heads commit to the base data) and isolate the cure: re-initializing only the query–key slices restores learnability (6/6) while the value slices do nothing (0/6). We prove the mechanism in a controlled gated-attention model, where occupation forces a finite deadline whose consequences need no mixing assumption. Completed: SGD’s noise fails the fluctuation–dissipation test, so we install one and anneal, melt and pin circuits on schedule. Frozen factors predict never-run combinations to 1–8%. Scope: conjunction circuits in transformers to 1.4B, two families.

1 Introduction: training has a statics; it is missing its kinetics

A substantial body of theory now describes learning in equilibrium terms. Singular learning theory characterizes training stages as phase transitions of a Bayesian free energy [1, 2, 3]; data-mixing thresholds have been derived as capacity-allocation optima [4]; grokking has been modeled as a first-order transition [5] and as thermal escape from a metastable state [6]. This is, in the language of materials science, the equilibrium phase diagram of training: which phases exist and which is preferred.

A phase diagram, however, answers none of the questions a practitioner asks. When will this capability appear? How fast will it grow, and can it be accelerated? Until when can it still be learned — and why does a network that has trained too long on the wrong data lose the ability to learn it at all [7]? Which circuit will a given perturbation destroy first? These are questions about rates, and a free energy is not a rate. Metallurgy needed a second diagram — the time–temperature–transformation (TTT) diagram — before phase knowledge became process control. Training does not yet have one.

This paper constructs that missing kinetics. Its single object of study is the nucleation rate of a computational circuit,

J=N⏟sites×ν⏟attempt freq.×σ⁡(c)⏟supersaturation×e−β​K⏟barrier−D⏟destruction,J\;=\;\underbrace{N}_{\text{sites}}\times\underbrace{\nu}_{\text{attempt freq.}}\times\underbrace{\sigma(c)}_{\text{supersaturation}}\times\underbrace{e^{-\beta K}}_{\text{barrier}}\;-\;\underbrace{D}_{\text{destruction}}, (1)

derived once from the stochastic dynamics of SGD (§2–§4) and then read three ways. Read forward — raising the drive σ\sigma past a floor — it is capability emergence, with a derived clock that dates arrival before the capability is measurable (§6). Read backward — as the site term NN is consumed by training itself — it is loss of plasticity, supplied with the quantitative law, horizon, mechanism, and repair that the plasticity literature identifies as missing (§7). And completed — injecting the temperature that SGD provably lacks — it becomes process control: annealing, selective dissolution, and quench-and-release schedules for individual circuits (§8). Every factor in Eq. (1) is measured independently, frozen, and tested on never-run combinations (§9); every section of this paper either measures one factor or reads the equation in one direction.

Such a construction earns its keep only if it pays out on problems the field already cares about, in the field’s own language. It pays out on three. Loss of plasticity is a recognized open problem: the phenomenon is established in Nature [7], the warm-starting puzzle [8] stands, and the causes literature is explicitly partial — intervening on any single proposed mechanism is insufficient [9]. What exists are remedies without a law, a timetable, or a located mechanism; §7 supplies each, quantitatively. Capability-level data scheduling: data-mixing methods [10, 11, 12] optimize loss, not which capabilities form; the floor, the clock, and the shelf life answer “for this mix and this size, will capability X emerge, when, and what is the deadline to still get it.” Emergence early-warning: frontier safety frameworks poll evaluations and react [13]; the precursor readout dates arrival while the capability itself is flat at baseline.

Scope, stated up front. Two model families (Pythia [14], OLMo [15] — the public suites with dense early checkpoints), scales to 1.4B, mechanism-level capabilities plus one task-level demonstration, causal constants from a controlled continued-training regime whose structure (not constants) is the claim — with the central causal results additionally reproduced from random initialization; and one explicitly unproved mathematical premise (Assumption 1) that is flagged wherever it is used.

2 The rate equation, forced step by step

We separate throughout what is cited (established results we do not re-prove), what is proved here (under stated assumptions), and what is measured. The derivation chain is short and each step forces the next.

Step 1 (cited): minibatch SGD, in the diffusion regime, is an SDE.

With minibatches, the update is the full gradient plus zero-mean noise; in the diffusion-approximation regime (small steps, locally Gaussian batch noise) SGD is approximated by d​θ=−∇L​(θ)​d​t+2​ε​Σ​(θ)​d​Wd\theta=-\nabla L(\theta)\,dt+\sqrt{2\varepsilon\,\Sigma(\theta)}\,dW with explicit weak-error bounds [16, 17]. Production optimizers (Adam, clipping, schedules) deform this SDE without removing its two load-bearing features — drift plus state-dependent noise — but we make no stronger claim: the regime condition is part of the theory’s stated scope (§12), and all causal constants are measured under plain SGD/AdamW where the approximation is controlled.

Step 2: why the barrier is exponential in KK — two independent foundations.

(A) Computational — proven complexity theory for the tested task class. For the family our premise tests instantiate — KK-wise conjunctions none of whose strict subsets carries signal, a property proved exactly for our apparatus in Lemma 1 — the exponential cost in KK is a theorem of learning theory, not an ansatz. Any statistical-query algorithm solving the (n,k)(n,k)-sparse parity problem with TT queries of tolerance τ\tau must satisfy T/τ2≥Ω⁡(nk)T/\tau^{2}\geq\Omega(n^{k}) [18, 19]; gradient methods with bounded gradient precision fall within the SQ framework (see the reduction discussed in 20, App. A.1 and references therein), and SGD provably operates near this limit, learning kk-parities in nO⁡(k)n^{O(k)} steps in the architectures where the guarantee is established [20]. Complementing the cost bound, the staircase and leap theorems [21, 22] prove the dichotomy on which our rate-determining-step analysis rests: targets whose monomials each add at most one new coordinate (subset signal at every stage) are SGD-learnable in O⁡(d)O(d) samples — an exact iff-characterization in the mean-field regime — while a leap of size ℓ\ell costs Θ~​(dmax⁡(ℓ−1,1))\tilde{\Theta}(d^{\max(\ell-1,1)}) online-SGD steps where proven (Gaussian nested-monomial targets under layer-wise training; CSQ lower bounds in general; conjectured for vanilla SGD, with the leap-2 case established for standard minibatch SGD by 23). These theorems govern the task class at large ambient dimension and in stated training regimes; our apparatus is a small-dimension member of the class whose defining no-subset-signal property holds exactly (Lemma 1), and training is single-pass throughout (batch reuse can evade the leap barrier [24]).

What the theorems fix, and what they do not. They fix the form — cost exponential in the number of jointly-required parts — not the constant. In the nkn^{k} scaling, nn counts candidate coordinates over which the relevant support must be found; it is not a vocabulary size, and no reading of the bound assigns β\beta a universal value. Written as eβe^{\beta} per part, β\beta is therefore a logarithm of an effective candidate pool, to be measured per system exactly as an activation energy is measured, not derived, in chemical kinetics. The measured values are informative on precisely this point: in the toy the per-part cost is β^=1.75\hat{\beta}=1.75 (summed family) and ≥2.40\geq 2.40 (parity family), i.e. effective pools of ≈6\approx 6 and ≥11\geq 11 — the scale of the local window the design makes relevant, and far below the full context, showing the search is structured rather than blind. On real models the clock’s β≈0.23\beta\approx 0.23 corresponds to an effective pool near unity: real circuit formation is not a blind combinatorial search at all, which is exactly what the staged picture of §10 predicts — cheap subset-signal-bearing stages first, leaving a small, heavily guided residual joint step. Consistently, per-part costs measured on real models by other protocols are of the same modest order and vary with circuit and regime (≈0.23\approx 0.23 from the clock; 0.470.47–0.620.62 from regeneration; ≈1.0\approx 1.0 from direct-KK control in prior work [25]) — a family- and circuit-indexed material constant, as the theory says it must be, and not a universal number the theorems could have supplied. (B) Physical — the nucleation reading, conditional on mixing. For a diffusion of Step 1’s form, the rate of a rare transition out of a metastable basin is, to leading exponential order, J≍exp(−ΔS/ε)J\asymp\exp(-\Delta S/\varepsilon), with Δ​S\Delta S the quasipotential action of the least-improbable escape path — Freidlin–Wentzell [26, 27]; Kramers in the reversible case [28]. Given mixing on the formation timescale (Assumption 1), large-deviation theory leaves no alternative leading-order form. Only this leg requires that assumption, and only this leg supplies the thermodynamic vocabulary — temperature, supersaturation, melting — and hence the control operations of §8. Rigorous escape-time and threshold analyses for online SGD exist in adjacent settings and scale exactly as this picture requires: sample complexity Nmax⁡(1,k−1)N^{\max(1,k-1)} for information exponent kk, with stretched-exponential trapping below threshold [29]. Three gaps between the classical theorems and production training are named rather than hidden: batch noise is not asymptotically small (the small-noise limit is a regime condition, whose diagnostic — memorylessness — is itself measured); adaptive optimizers carry moment state beyond a θ\theta-diffusion (our controlled measurements run under AdamW, so the measured signatures already include this deformation); and the landscape evolves during training (the quasi-stationarity clause of Assumption 1).

Step 3 (proved here): for a KK-part circuit, Δ​S=β​K\Delta S=\beta K.

This is the mathematical core of the paper — the point where the generic exponential acquires its content — and it occupies §4.

Step 4 (measured): what multiplies the exponential.

The prefactor factorizes as sites ×\times attempt frequency ×\times supersaturation under conditional independence (a mean-field approximation whose regime of validity, and measured breakdown at the boundary, are quantified in §9). The supersaturation has the measured form σ⁡(c)∝(c−c0)γ\sigma(c)\propto(c-c_{0})^{\gamma} above a floor concentration c0c_{0} and is zero below it (§6). The destruction term DD has two components with different supports: a reversion drift on sub-critical embryos (always present — it is what the drive must overcome, and what sets the floor), and a knockdown component acting on formed structure, which is Arrhenius in an injected temperature and dormant at native settings and practical learning rates (§8).

The non-equilibrium branch (diagnosis cited; test and prescription ours).

That SGD is out of equilibrium — broken detailed balance, anisotropic state-dependent noise — is established [30, 31], and we do not claim the diagnosis. What we add is the operational step: a fluctuation–dissipation qualification test that any candidate “temperature knob” must pass, the measured result that all six native SGD knobs fail it (§5), and the prescription that follows — the drive is data, and a true temperature, if wanted for control, must be injected (§8).

3 Methods and apparatus

All experiments fall into three apparatus classes; every number in the paper traces to one of them, and every protocol below was frozen (with pass/kill criteria) before the corresponding formal runs.

Controlled toys (premise tests, EK suite; nose/melt/quench). Models are 2-layer GPT-NeoX transformers (hidden 256, 4–16 heads, MLP 4×4\times, rotary 25%), trained with AdamW (lr 5×10−45\times 10^{-4}, β=(0.9,0.95)\beta=(0.9,0.95), weight decay 0.010.01, gradient clip 1.01.0), batch 64, from seeded random initialization. Conjunction task (EK-1/2/3): sequences of length 64 over a 64-token vocabulary follow a peaked Markov chain; with probability ν\nu (the drive) a position is replaced by the sum mod 64 of the tokens at the KK fixed offsets — the KK-part target. The probe is next-token accuracy on fully-enabled sequences (256-sequence batch, evaluated every 10–25 steps); t∗t^{*} = first crossing of 0.50.5 (crossings at 0.3/0.5/0.70.3/0.5/0.7 recorded). Open-loop query-parity task (EK-4/5): sequences of length 96 over {0,1}\{0,1\} plus query tokens; at query positions (gaps ≥W+3\geq W{+}3, guaranteeing every window contains only raw i.i.d. bits — no feedback channel) the next token is the parity of the KK bits at KK of the WW window slots, the remaining slots being distractors. Parity makes every strict subset of the relevant bits exactly independent of the target. Score = accuracy at answer positions (chance 0.50.5); t∗t^{*} = first crossing of 0.750.75 (crossings at 0.6/0.75/0.90.6/0.75/0.9 recorded). Missing-parts grid (EK-5): a neutral substrate (8,000 steps of constant-answer queries — builds the readout, zero parts) is followed by a +1+1 curriculum, each stage trained to completion (score ≥0.9\geq 0.9 on three consecutive evaluations, plus 500 consolidation steps) and checkpointed; grid cells load the ss-part substrate and train the KK-part task with a 70/30 task/maintenance query mix (maintenance sustains the built parts; both the 30% and 0% variants are reported, with their respective identified artifacts, in §4.4); slot roles are randomly permuted per seed so that slot difficulty averages out within every cell. Injected bath (§8): isotropic Gaussian weight noise of per-step scale 2​T⋅lr\sqrt{2T\cdot\mathrm{lr}} added to all parameters — the qualified temperature of Definition 2.

Statistics. Waiting times are censoring-aware throughout: medians count censored runs as +∞+\infty (the Kaplan–Meier median, since all censoring occurs at the budget end; reported as undefined below 50% formation), and means use the shifted-exponential maximum-likelihood estimator with right-censoring. The estimators were validated directly by rerunning every censored cell at doubled budget: the KM medians predicted the extended-budget measurements exactly in all three cases (the naive median-of-formed had been 15–19% low). Calibration (smoke) seeds are excluded from all analyses.

Public-checkpoint observation (§6). Mechanism-level probes are single forward passes at public Pythia and OLMo checkpoints in fp32 with eager attention (a stated numerical precondition: bf16 softmax underflow collapses the scores). Induction score = prefix-matching attention on repeated random tokens [32] (best head); precursor score = previous-token attention (best head); task probes are logit-difference accuracies with train/eval-disjoint content. t∗t^{*} = first 0.5-crossing, log-interpolated between checkpoints; thresholds 0.3/0.5/0.7×0.3/0.5/0.7\times linear/log interpolation give held-out median errors 4.4–13.0% in all six variants. Clock constants were fit on five Pythia models, frozen, and only then evaluated on held-out models.

Controlled continued training and from-scratch reproduction (§6–§7). Substrates are public Pythia models (70M–410M) or random initializations of the same architecture. The drive is supplied as repeated-token passages mixed into plain text at per-batch concentration cc; the switch replaces the mix at an experimenter-chosen step; aging trains SS steps on plain data before the switch; resets restore named weight groups (attention / MLP / embeddings) of an aged substrate to young values; the revival sweep raises cc on a dead substrate. Arm sizes: switch/shelf/reset n=5n=5; floor sweep 0/12 and 4/5 at the critical concentrations; others n=2n=2–3 as flagged in §12. Every number is recomputable from released per-experiment JSON files and scripts.

4 The mathematical core: a combinatorial barrier and its clock

This section states the assumptions, proves the barrier and clock laws, and reports the experiments that test each assumption separately. The logical status of every claim is marked, and the ledger now has three grades rather than one. Proved outright: the no-partial-credit structure of the test apparatus (Lemma 1 — Assumption 2 is exact by construction there), and the exponential cost in KK for the task class, which stands on the query-complexity and leap theorems of §2(A) independently of any stochastic-analysis premise. Conditional theorems: the nucleation-form propositions below, exact given Assumptions 1–3; of these, only the physical reading still leans on the unproven mixing clause, which no result of ours can currently discharge for transformer SGD. Measured: every remaining premise, each falsifiable against a concrete alternative and tested in a dedicated preregistered experiment (§4.4) independently of the conclusions it licenses.

4.1 Setting and definitions

Definition 1 (Circuit, parts, order parameter).

A circuit is a set of KK jointly necessary computational parts (attention-head functions) whose conjunction implements a capability. KK is defined operationally as the size of the minimal causal part set: the smallest set of components each individually necessary at a just-post-ignition checkpoint (single-component ablation destroys the capability), machine-counted by the engine (§9), not assigned by hand. Its order parameter ϕ⁡(t)∈[0,1]\phi(t)\in[0,1] is the normalized completeness (probe) score, and its formation time t∗t^{*} is the first 0.50.5-crossing of ϕ\phi (threshold-robustness is quantified in §6).

Assumption 1 (SDE regime and mixing — the open frontier).

On the formation timescale, (a) the SDE approximation of Step 1 holds, and (b) the dynamics within the pre-formation basin is sufficiently mixing that the quasi-stationary escape theory of Freidlin and Wentzell [26] applies. Part (b) is not proved for transformer SGD; it is the single unproved premise on which the propositions below are conditional, we flag it rather than hide it, and §12 states what would change if it were established (every proposition below becomes an unconditional theorem).

Assumption 2 (Simultaneous joint alignment).

Formation of a KK-part circuit requires the KK sub-alignments to be present simultaneously in an attempt window; partial progress on a strict subset does not accumulate into the crossing. (Empirically discriminated from the alternative — sequential, “archivable” assembly — in §4.4: the two models make opposite predictions, and the data select this one.)

Lemma 1 (Zero drift on subset-supported directions — exact in the test apparatus).

In the parity apparatus of §3, let the window bits (bi)(b_{i}) be i.i.d. uniform and independent of the remaining context ZZ, let RR (|R|=K|R|=K) be the relevant slots, and for any SS with R⊈SR\not\subseteq S let 𝒜S=σ⁡((bi)i∈S,Z)\mathcal{A}_{S}=\sigma((b_{i})_{i\in S},Z) be the information available to a strict-subset feature. Then: (a) 𝔼⁡[Y∣𝒜S]=12\mathbb{E}[Y\mid\mathcal{A}_{S}]=\tfrac{1}{2} a.s.; (b) among all 𝒜S\mathcal{A}_{S}-measurable predictors, the population cross-entropy is globally minimized at chance (p≡12p\equiv\tfrac{1}{2}) — no descent below chance exists anywhere in the subset-supported predictor class; (c) (Fourier form) the target’s expansion over the window bits consists of the single character χR\chi_{R}: 𝔼⁡[(2​Y−1)​χT]=0\mathbb{E}[(2Y{-}1)\chi_{T}]=0 for every T≠RT\neq R, so the population gradient’s correlation with any partial character vanishes identically; (d) (stationarity) on the chance manifold, the projection of the population loss gradient onto the 𝒜S\mathcal{A}_{S}-measurable function subspace is zero, for every strict subset SS simultaneously. Assumption 2 is therefore not an idealization in the apparatus but exact by construction, at the level of the dynamics and not merely of the information.

Proof.

(a) Y=⨁i∈S∩Rbi⊕⨁j∈R∖SbjY=\bigoplus_{i\in S\cap R}b_{i}\oplus\bigoplus_{j\in R\setminus S}b_{j}; the second factor is uniform and independent of 𝒜S\mathcal{A}_{S} since R∖S≠∅R\setminus S\neq\emptyset. (b) Conditioning on 𝒜S\mathcal{A}_{S}, 𝔼⁡[ℓ⁡(p,Y)∣𝒜S]=12​ℓ​(p,1)+12​ℓ​(p,0)\mathbb{E}[\ell(p,Y)\mid\mathcal{A}_{S}]=\tfrac{1}{2}\ell(p,1)+\tfrac{1}{2}\ell(p,0), uniquely minimized at p=12p=\tfrac{1}{2}; take expectations. (c) 2​Y−1=χR2Y-1=\chi_{R}, and characters are orthonormal under the uniform measure. (d) For any 𝒜S\mathcal{A}_{S}-measurable function-space direction gg, the cross-entropy functional gradient component is 𝔼⁡[(p−Y)​g]=𝔼⁡[(p−𝔼⁡[Y∣𝒜S])​g]=𝔼⁡[(p−12)​g]\mathbb{E}[(p-Y)g]=\mathbb{E}[(p-\mathbb{E}[Y\mid\mathcal{A}_{S}])g]=\mathbb{E}[(p-\tfrac{1}{2})g], which vanishes at p≡12p\equiv\tfrac{1}{2}. ∎

Remark 1 (Dynamical reading).

Population drift can neither build nor be rewarded for any strict-subset feature (b, d); all progress toward the target flows through the joint-KK channel (c); minibatch fluctuation is the only mover of subset features and is unrewarded. This is precisely the “no feedback from guessed indices unless the subset is exactly correct” property that Barak et al. [20] identify for sparse parity, here established for our apparatus by construction — the leap-KK property [22] instantiated.

Remark 2.

For real circuits, Assumption 2 is an empirical property rather than a construction, and it is measured, not presumed: pre-ignition, the target capability’s own curve is flat to slopes of 10−610^{-6}–10−510^{-5}/step and a placebo sweep of 200 random heads carries no predictive signal (42.5% error = guessing; §6) — the behavioral face of “no partial credit.” Real assembly is staged precisely where partial credit does exist (parts with independent utility form early, §10); the assumption governs the rate-limiting final step, which is where it is tested.

Assumption 3 (Part independence, with a measured failure domain).

Away from the capacity wall, the KK sub-alignment events in an attempt window are approximately independent. This is the mean-field idealization of the theory; its failure is itself measurable (Corollary 1) and is measured in §4.4.

4.2 The barrier law

Proposition 1 (Additivity of the combinatorial barrier).

Under Assumptions 1–3, let the ii-th sub-alignment be a rare event of per-attempt probability pi≍e−si/εp_{i}\asymp e^{-s_{i}/\varepsilon}. Then the per-attempt formation probability satisfies

P(formation in one attempt)=∏i=1Kpi≍exp(−1ε∑i=1Ksi),P(\text{formation in one attempt})\;=\;\prod_{i=1}^{K}p_{i}\;\asymp\;\exp\!\Big(-\tfrac{1}{\varepsilon}\sum_{i=1}^{K}s_{i}\Big),

so the escape action is additive, Δ​S=∑isi\Delta S=\sum_{i}s_{i}; for exchangeable parts (si≡ss_{i}\equiv s),

J∝ν​e−β​K,β:=s/ε.J\;\propto\;\nu\,e^{-\beta K},\qquad\beta:=s/\varepsilon.
Proof.

By Assumption 2 the formation event in an attempt window is the intersection ⋂iEi\bigcap_{i}E_{i} of the KK sub-alignment events; by Assumption 3 the probability of the intersection is the product of the probabilities. Taking logarithms, the large-deviation exponents add — the elementary additivity of independent rare-event costs that underlies Cramér’s and Sanov’s theorems [27]. Exchangeability collapses the sum to s​KsK. Under Assumption 1, the escape rate inherits this action through the Freidlin–Wentzell principle (Step 2), giving J∝ν​e−β​KJ\propto\nu e^{-\beta K} with the attempt frequency ν\nu as prefactor. ∎

Remark 3.

The mathematical content is deliberately elementary; the scientific content is the identification (Assumption 2) and the independence idealization (Assumption 3), both of which are tested as separate experimental questions in §4.4 rather than bundled into a fit. This is why the exponential-in-KK form is derived, not chosen: given the premises, no other form is available, and the premises are checked independently of the conclusion.

Corollary 1 (Deviation from linearity measures part dependence).

If the parts share a common enabling cause (positive association), P⁡(⋂iEi)≥∏iP⁡(Ei)P(\bigcap_{i}E_{i})\geq\prod_{i}P(E_{i}), so Δ​S≤s​K\Delta S\leq sK: the barrier grows sublinearly in KK. If forming parts consume a shared resource (negative interaction, e.g. capacity near the wall), the barrier grows superlinearly. The measured departure of ln⁡t∗\ln t^{*} from linearity in KK is therefore a direct, signed measure of part dependence — the theory’s own error bar, not an anomaly.

4.3 The clock law

Proposition 2 (Memoryless waiting and the precursor clock).

Under Assumption 1, the normalized escape (formation) time is asymptotically exponentially distributed with mean ∝1/J\propto 1/J [33, 34]. For a composition of KK exchangeable parts and its single-part precursor driven by the same stream, the exact ratio is

𝔼​tcomp∗𝔼​tprec∗=AprecAcomp​eβ⁡(K−1),\frac{\mathbb{E}\,t^{*}_{\rm comp}}{\mathbb{E}\,t^{*}_{\rm prec}}\;=\;\frac{A_{\rm prec}}{A_{\rm comp}}\,e^{\beta(K-1)},

where A=N​νA=N\nu collects each circuit’s prefactor (sites ×\times attempt frequency). Under the additional prefactor-cancellation assumption Aprec≈AcompA_{\rm prec}\approx A_{\rm comp} (A3, stated and tested below), the clock C⁡(K)=eβ⁡(K−1)C(K)=e^{\beta(K-1)} is a derived constant: measuring the precursor’s arrival dates the composition’s arrival before the composition exists.

Proof.

The exponential limit law for exit times from a metastable basin under small noise is classical [33]; mean exit time ≍\asymp inverse rate is the content of metastability theory in the same regime [34]. The ratio of means is then the ratio of inverse rates, which is (Aprec/Acomp)​eβ⁡(K−1)({A_{\rm prec}}/{A_{\rm comp}})\,e^{\beta(K-1)} by Proposition 1; A3 reduces it to eβ⁡(K−1)e^{\beta(K-1)}. ∎

Remark 4 (The prefactor ratio is counted, not assumed).

The prefactor is where a skeptic should push — “a single head and a multi-head composition have search spaces differing by orders of magnitude” — so we count it rather than assume it. The prefactor of a rate-limiting step is A=Nsites​(missing structure)×νA=N_{\rm sites}(\text{missing structure})\times\nu, where NsitesN_{\rm sites} counts eligible configurations of the missing structure only: the missing-parts grid (EK-5, §4.4) measures directly that built structure is kinetically invisible, so what enters is not the circuit’s total configuration space but the remainder’s. For the clock, the precursor’s missing structure is one part among the Hℓ1H_{\ell_{1}} heads of its layer, and the composition’s post-precursor missing structure is one part among the Hℓ2H_{\ell_{2}} heads of the reading layer:

AprecAcomp=Hℓ1Hℓ2= 1for uniform architectures (equal heads per layer, as in Pythia and OLMo).\frac{A_{\rm prec}}{A_{\rm comp}}\;=\;\frac{H_{\ell_{1}}}{H_{\ell_{2}}}\;=\;1\quad\text{for uniform architectures (equal heads per layer, as in Pythia and OLMo).}

The pair-counting intuition (Acomp∝H1​H2A_{\rm comp}\propto H_{1}H_{2}, or more generally a (HK)\binom{H}{K} combinatorial factor) prices forming both parts jointly from nothing — that is the s=0s{=}0 column of the grid, and it is carried by the barrier e−β​Ke^{-\beta K}, not by the clock’s prefactor. This is not a verbal distinction but a measured one, and the missing-parts grid is precisely the experiment that decides it: were the prefactor to carry a combinatorial factor over the whole part set, cells with more already-built parts would search a systematically different space and rows of fixed missing count could not be flat — yet they are, to 1.191.19–1.371.37 at K−s=3K{-}s{=}3 across K=3,4,5K=3,4,5 (§4.4), with overlapping bootstrap intervals. Two further measurements support the counting model with no new assumptions: sites enter the rate linearly (EK-3, deep-barrier slope −1.25-1.25); and two different circuits (K=2K{=}2, C=1.24C{=}1.24; K=4K{=}4, C=2.1C{=}2.1) are consistent with one β≈0.23\beta\approx 0.23 — two equations, one constant, impossible under freely varying prefactors. The model is falsifiable where it should be: architectures with unequal per-layer head counts are predicted to shift the clock by ln⁡(Hℓ1/Hℓ2)\ln(H_{\ell_{1}}/H_{\ell_{2}}), a concrete out-of-family test. Residual imbalance is absorbed into the effective β\beta, part of why β\beta is family-indexed.

Remark 5 (What is fit and what is not, and the range-of-KK question).

β\beta is a family-dependent effective constant (the general ∑isi\sum_{i}s_{i} form explains its variation across capabilities and families); it is fit once, on-axis and then frozen. The clock’s form is derived; its prospective, frozen-constant validation on held-out models (median 5% error, 6/6, cross-family) is reported in §6. We are explicit about the dynamic range: our own direct-KK measurements span K=2..4K=2..4, over which exponential, power, and linear fits are locally indistinguishable (R2R^{2} 0.980/0.978/0.989) — too narrow for model selection by fit alone, which is exactly why the premises, not the curve, carry the argument (§4.4). Wide-range evidence exists in an adjacent literature: for kk-sparse parity — the canonical task in which no strict subset carries signal, i.e. a pure joint-alignment problem — SGD’s time-to-learn scales as dΘ⁡(k)d^{\Theta(k)} [20]: ln⁡t∗\ln t^{*} linear in kk with per-part cost ln⁡d\ln d, the additive combinatorial barrier over a kk-range far wider than ours. This is Proposition 1 instantiated in an independent setting, not our data; extending our own ladder to K≥5K\geq 5 with a subset-signal-free design is the single highest-value additional experiment this theory admits.

4.4 Testing the premises, not just the conclusion

Each assumption above is the target of a dedicated experiment (design frozen before running; the EK suite):

Statistics are censoring-aware throughout: medians count censored runs as +∞+\infty (the Kaplan–Meier median here, since all censoring occurs at the budget end), and means use the shifted-exponential maximum-likelihood estimator with right-censoring; cells with <<50% formation are reported as undefined rather than estimated. The estimators were validated directly: rerunning every censored cell at doubled budget (to 92–100% formation), the censoring-corrected KM medians predicted the extended-budget measurements exactly in all three cases, and the MLE means to 0.2–10%, where the naive median-of-formed had been 15–19% low. K=1K{=}1 cells form at the evaluation-grid floor (t∗≤25t^{*}\leq 25) and are therefore reported only as bounds, never entered into fits.

(EK-1) Memorylessness of waiting times [tests the premise of Prop. 2]. At fixed (K,ν)(K,\nu), the formation-time distribution over 60 seeds per cell spans the predicted crossover (Fig. 2a): at shallow barriers the waiting is nearly deterministic (raw κ≈220\kappa\approx 220, CV 0.07), and as the barrier deepens the shifted-tail shape parameter falls to κ=2.0\kappa=2.0 and then plateaus at the memoryless limit — κ=1.2\kappa=1.2 and 1.31.3 at the two deepest barriers (60/60 formed at extended budget) — the exponential regime, exactly where the clock law needs it, and stable once reached. (Cell labels: the deep-barrier cells here are the summed design’s nominal K=3K{=}3, which the discriminator below shows solves the task by a two-part shortcut. The measured claim is unaffected — what is established is that waiting becomes memoryless once formation is barrier-dominated, a statement about the kinetics and not about the part count — but we do not attach a part count to these cells.) Consistent prior evidence: κ≈80\kappa\approx 80 at full batch →\to κ→1\kappa\to 1 under minibatch noise [25]. Logical status: exponential waiting is a necessary condition of Assumption 1(b), so EK-1 is a consistency test that could have falsified the assumption and did not — it is not, and is not offered as, a proof of mixing. Regime diagnosis: κ\kappa also arbitrates between the two proven mechanisms available to the computational leg. Barak et al. [20] show that at population scale SGD amplifies a deterministic Fourier-gap signal of size γ=Θ(n−(k−1)/2)\gamma=\Theta(n^{-(k-1)/2}) — progress hidden but not random — while at batch sizes far below the ∼nk\sim n^{k} needed to resolve γ\gamma per step, the search is fluctuation-dominated. The two mechanisms share the same nΘ⁡(k)n^{\Theta(k)} cost (the SQ bound is mechanism-blind) but differ in waiting-time shape: deterministic amplification gives κ≫1\kappa\gg 1, fluctuation-driven escape gives κ→1\kappa\to 1. Our measured κ\kappa spectrum (≈\approx220 at shallow barriers →\to 1.2–1.3 at deep ones, at batch 64) locates the apparatus in the fluctuation-dominated regime precisely where the nucleation reading applies — and simultaneously shows the crossover toward the deterministic regime at shallow barriers, reconciling the two literatures rather than contradicting either.

(EK-2) Additivity, and a measured pathway change [tests Prop. 1 and Cor. 1]. The same nested part set is assembled into K=2,3K=2,3 at fixed drive across three widths (Fig. 2b). We report this family in full, including a contamination we found by direct probing and which withdraws part of it.

In the summed design the target at an enabled position is the sum of the KK preceding tokens; when two consecutive positions are both enabled, subtracting the two relations gives st=2​st−1−st−K−1s_{t}=2s_{t-1}-s_{t-K-1} — an algebraic shortcut requiring only two attention targets, independent of KK. It is a second solution to the same task: it agrees with the true KK-sum wherever the recurrence holds and disagrees where it is broken. A discriminating probe (scoring positions whose predecessor is not enabled, so that the shortcut is wrong and the true sum still right) settles which solution each cell learns. The verdict is sharp: at K=2K{=}2 the network learns the true sum (broken/valid accuracy ratio 0.940.94, n=8n{=}8), while at K=3K{=}3 and K=4K{=}4 it learns the shortcut (ratios 0.110.11 and 0.030.03; broken-position accuracy 0.0600.060 and 0.0150.015 against a chance level of 0.0160.016). We therefore withdraw the summed family’s K≥3K\geq 3 cells as barrier measurements: β^=ln⁡(t3∗/t2∗)=1.75\hat{\beta}=\ln(t^{*}_{3}/t^{*}_{2})=1.75 compares a shortcut-formation time to a true-sum formation time and is not a clean per-part increment. The trustworthy per-part cost is the parity family’s (≥\geq11×\times; §4.4, EK-4), and the reason for the gap is now mechanistic rather than mysterious: the summed design admits a shortcut and the parity design provably does not.

The pathway change is itself a measured result, and it disposes of what previously looked like an anomaly. K=4K{=}4 forming faster than K=3K{=}3 (1175 vs. 1738 in replication; 1138 vs. 1725 originally) is not a violation of additivity: from K=3K{=}3 upward both cells run on the same KK-independent shortcut, whose cost does not grow with KK, so the ladder flattens rather than climbing. This is textbook parallel-pathway competition — kinetic versus thermodynamic product — with the crossover located at K=3K{=}3: below it the true solution is the cheaper route, above it the two-part shortcut is, and the system takes whichever barrier is lower, not whichever solution is more accurate. The picture makes a sharp prediction, which we then tested: if every cell from K=3K{=}3 upward runs on the same KK-independent route, formation times must plateau rather than continue climbing. Measured (8 seeds per cell): 300300, 17381738, 11751175, 938938, 962962 steps at K=2,3,4,5,6K=2,3,4,5,6, with the discriminator ratio 0.940.94 at K=2K{=}2 and 0.11,0.03,0.03,0.030.11,0.03,0.03,0.03 thereafter. The ladder flattens exactly where the discriminator says the route changes, and the size of the effect is not marginal: an additive ladder continued from the true-sum cells would place K=6K{=}6 near 3×1053\times 10^{5} steps, against 962962 measured — a factor of 350350. A confirmed prediction of a pathway crossover is stronger evidence for parallel-route kinetics than the original clean ladder would have been for additivity. Our first hypothesis for this cell, a metastable partial-sum intermediate (Ostwald staging), was tested by probing every partial sum during training and refuted: 0/8 seeds showed a partial-sum plateau (peak partial accuracy 0.030.03 against chance 0.0160.016). We report that failure because it is what forced the correct explanation.

What the width sweep still shows, within the uncontaminated K=2K{=}2 cells: shrinking width toward the capacity wall inflates the barrier (t2∗t^{*}_{2}: 300→900→2000300\to 900\to 2000 from d=256d{=}256 to 9696 to 6464, a 6.7×6.7\times capacity penalty) — the capacity-competition side of Cor. 1, measured on cells the discriminator certifies as true-sum solutions.

(EK-3) Product law versus bottleneck [tests Assumption 2]. Simultaneous joint alignment predicts rate ∝\propto sites in the rare-event regime; sequential/archivable assembly predicts a bottleneck (max) law whose site-dependence should strengthen as the drive stops binding. A sites(heads) ×\times drive(ν\nu) grid decides (Fig. 2c): at the memoryless point the log–log slope of t∗t^{*} against head count is −1.25-1.25 (confirmed uncensored at extended budget, 8/8) — rate proportional to sites, the product law; in the drift-limited cells the slope collapses to ≈0\approx 0 — no site statistics where formation is not a rare event. (As in EK-1, the deep-barrier cells are the summed design’s nominal K=3K{=}3; the site-proportionality is a statement about the kinetics of a barrier-dominated formation event, with no part count attached.) The bottleneck law predicts the opposite pattern (site-dependence strongest at high drive) and is refuted in both regimes. Consistent prior evidence: J∝N⋅rJ\propto N\cdot r, R2R^{2} 0.97 [25].

(EK-5) The missing-parts grid [tests additivity through its sharpest fingerprint]. If barriers add, formation time depends only on the number of missing parts, never on the circuit’s total size: a substrate holding ss of KK parts (pre-built by staged curriculum, each stage trained to completion — partially formed parts do not count, a threshold measured in prior work [25]) waits only for the remaining K−sK-s to align jointly. A (K,s)(K,s) grid over K=2..5K=2..5, s=0..4s=0..4 (46 cells, 8–16 seeds each, slot roles randomized per seed, criteria preregistered) confirms the fingerprint where it is cleanest: at fixed K−s=3K{-}s=3 the cell medians for K=3,4,5K=3,4,5 agree to 1.19–1.37 (4550/6225/5412 steps; bootstrap 95% intervals share a common overlap, [1275,8050][1275,8050]), and at K−s=4K{-}s=4 to 1.08–1.34 (common overlap [4912,14412][4912,14412]) — a five-part circuit missing three waits as long as a three-part circuit missing three, though its total barrier is far larger. The alternatives fail characteristically: an energetic (cluster-size) barrier requires within-row growth with KK (none observed; row maxima are interior), and sequential accumulation requires arithmetic row spacing (measured spacings are not arithmetic). Two protocol artifacts were caught, mechanism-traced, and controlled: a copy-task maintenance stream interferes specifically with s=1s{=}1 cells (removing it restores 8/8 formation and a >>2×\times lower median), while zero maintenance lets built parts decay in high-ss cells, in proportion to their exposure time — under per-cell clean protocols the shallow-row spread is 1.86, and the deepest measured row is flat under both protocols (1.13 and 1.33). A window-width sweep closed the last gap: apparent rung-height saturation at deep rows vanishes when distractor slots are replenished (rung ratio ×2.1→×3.9\times 2.1\to\times 3.9 from W=5W{=}5 to 66, exceeding the entire budget at W≥7W\geq 7) — a designed-in ceiling of the smallest window, not a failure of additivity (Fig. 1).

The regime map as a consistency check. Three independent measurements draw the same boundary: waiting is memoryless (κ→1\kappa\to 1) precisely in the cells where the site-product law holds (slope −1.25-1.25), and deterministic (κ≫1\kappa\gg 1) precisely where site statistics vanish (slope ≈0\approx 0). The nucleation theory’s signatures appear together, in its claimed domain — the barrier-dominated regime that real compositional circuits inhabit — and switch off together outside it. (A3, shared pace) Across from-scratch ladder seeds, successive stage increments are strongly co-scaled (corr=+0.89\mathrm{corr}=+0.89) — precisely the common mode the ratio clock cancels.

Near-wall breakdown of factorization (the 112% point, error growing as a power of floor distance) is reported with the synthesis in §9 — by Cor. 1 it is the predicted signature of part dependence at shared capacity, and it converts the law’s boundary from a caveat into a falsifiable commitment.

5 No intrinsic temperature: the fluctuation–dissipation qualification test

Equilibrium escape theory presumes a bath. Before Eq. (1) can be read as thermal nucleation, one must ask which, if any, of training’s native knobs supplies a temperature. We make the question operational.

Definition 2 (Temperature qualification).

A noise source qualifies as a temperature for the escape dynamics if it satisfies the fluctuation–dissipation structure of an equilibrium bath [35]: its covariance is (i) isotropic, (ii) independent of the current state (in particular, it does not vanish at loss minima), so that (iii) the stationary distribution it induces is the Gibbs measure of the loss at that temperature, and Kramers/Freidlin–Wentzell escape applies with ε=T\varepsilon=T.

This is a criterion, cited, not a theorem of ours; our contribution is to apply it as a qualification exam. Two clarifications delimit the claim. First, it concerns the equilibrium notion of temperature — the one under which Gibbs sampling and Kramers escape are licensed; non-equilibrium effective temperatures (noise temperatures, FDT-violation ratios) can of course be defined for SGD, and our statement is precisely that none of them earns the escape-theory role. Second, the verdict is empirical and unambiguous. Minibatch-gradient noise has covariance proportional to the per-sample gradient second moment: state-coupled (it dies where gradients die), highly anisotropic (covariance rank as low as ∼\sim1% [30]), and therefore fails (i)–(iii) structurally — the known result that SGD does not sample a Gibbs measure [30], sharpened recently to full thermodynamic irreversibility with the explicit warning that step size is not a temperature [31]. We tested all six native knobs (minibatch noise, learning rate, batch size, dropout, weight decay, and their clock-rescaled combinations) against Definition 2 in the controlled apparatus of §8: zero qualify. Learning rate is not even “partially” thermal: converting its noise amplification into an effective clock leaves a monotonic 60×60\times degradation and zero net barrier assistance — it is an anti-thermal amplifier, and its noise power is strongly state-dependent (measured factor 2.5×2.5\times between formed and plateau states for SGD noise; 72×72\times for dropout). This is consistent, not in tension, with the real-LM finding that within the igniting region learning rate simply accelerates ignition (§6): in both regimes the unified statement is that lr is a clock, never a temperature — it rescales time without ever supplying barrier assistance. Anti-thermal noise does not merely fail to help: because it is gradient-coupled, it selectively dismantles exactly the multi-part coincidences that Proposition 1 prices — measured as barrier-gated damage (high-KK circuits hurt ≈2.7×\approx 2.7\times more than low-KK on the dropout axis).

Two consequences organize the rest of the paper. First, the drive is data: with no thermal term available, the only state-decoupled generation knob in Eq. (1) is the supersaturation σ⁡(c)\sigma(c) — the concentration of capability-relevant statistics in the stream. Formation in native training is athermal, driven nucleation, and its control variable is the data mix (§6). Second, the missing term can be installed: an injected isotropic weight-noise bath passes the qualification by construction, and §8 shows that installing it buys exactly the control functions (anneal, dissolve, pin) that native training lacks. In prior work the injected bath was verified to restore a single (U,D)(U,D) pair reproducing drift, occupancy, and committor simultaneously [25].

6 Reading the equation forward: emergence

Forward means: hold a substrate fixed, raise the drive σ⁡(c)\sigma(c), and watch the generation term. The equation predicts a threshold (no nucleation below a supersaturation floor), a throttle (rate rising steeply above it), and a clock (the barrier ratio of Prop. 2). Each is confirmed, the clock prospectively.

Probes, protocols, and preregistration are specified in §3; mechanism-level probes make “emergence” unambiguous, and constants were frozen before any held-out model was measured.

6.1 The clock, prospectively validated

Fit C=1.241C=1.241 on five Pythia models (leave-one-out median 3%); froze constants; predicted six unseen models (five deduped-data variants and pythia-1b, outside the fitted scale range): 6/6 within the preregistered 25% band, median 5.0% (Fig. 3). Cross-family: OLMo-1B — different architecture, data, tokenizer — measures 1.244 against the frozen 1.241. A cheap variant reads a single attention score at step 512 (0.36% of training, target capability at baseline everywhere): 6/6, median 12.8%. No circularity, twice over: every prospective test used the human-known previous-token head from prior literature; the automatic engine (§9) is validated against these answers, not their source. And the prospective record concerns induction only, with constants frozen before any held-out model was measured; the cross-circuit unification of β\beta (induction with IOI, §9) is a separate, explicitly post-hoc consistency check and is nowhere counted as a prospective result. No alternative signal: pre-ignition, the target’s own curve is flat (slopes 10−610^{-6}–10−510^{-5}/step), and a placebo sweep shows 200 random heads predict at 42.5% error (= guessing) versus the causal precursor’s 8.7%. Where Lavie et al. [36] conclude softmax-attention emergence is intrinsically unpredictable and Baherwani et al. [37] that timing is initialization-random, these prospective results are a direct counterexample for the capability class covered here: the timing is predictable, from the precursor, because the barrier is combinatorial.

Mechanism dates behavior. Across 15/15 model–task pairs the mechanism ignites first; real-text in-context learning ignites simultaneously with the mechanism (ratios 0.93–0.97), strict exact-copy behavior lags ×\times1.27 (Fig. 4). A task-level few-shot skill (in-context label induction) shows the full ladder on public checkpoints: never below the capacity wall (70M flat through 143k steps), late and stretched at its edge (160M ∼\sim12,400), scale-consistent above it (410M: 3,933; 1B: 3,822), ∼\sim5×\times after the induction mechanism (Fig. 5). And on all choice-based probes the pre-ignition period is systematically below chance — an anti-phase reported as a robust correlational early-warning channel, not a proven mechanism: the direct causal test was inconclusive because the precursor is redundant (§11).

6.2 The floor: a supersaturation threshold, proved intensive

The floor is where the kinetic reading departs most sharply from the equilibrium one. Gu et al. [4] document a data-mixing threshold and attribute it to capacity allocation — an equilibrium answer (which phase wins the parameter budget). Equation (1) makes a stronger, kinetic claim: below a critical concentration the rate is suppressed beyond nucleation order — operationally zero for any subexponential token budget — and the threshold is a property of the per-step stream composition, not of any total.

Proposition 3 (The floor is a fold — from structure, with no functional form assumed).

Let ϕ∈[0,1]\phi\in[0,1] be the alignment order parameter (the normalized product of attention masses on the KK required slots, so ϕ=1\phi=1 iff every part is in place). Write the population drift as ϕ˙=c​G​(ϕ)−D⁡(ϕ)\dot{\phi}=c\,G(\phi)-D(\phi), target minus competitor. Then the following three properties — each derived, none postulated — suffice: (D1) the competitor’s drift is linear in ϕ\phi: D⁡(ϕ)=r​ϕD(\phi)=r\phi with r=K⁡(1−c)​λ′>0r=K(1-c)\lambda^{\prime}>0; (D2) the target’s drift vanishes super-linearly at the origin: GG is continuous on [0,1][0,1] with G⁡(ϕ)/ϕ→0G(\phi)/\phi\to 0 as ϕ→0+\phi\to 0^{+}; (D3) it vanishes again at completion and is bounded between: G⁡(1)=0G(1)=0, GG bounded, G>0G>0 on (0,1)(0,1). Let h⁡(ϕ):=G⁡(ϕ)/ϕh(\phi):=G(\phi)/\phi, extended by h⁡(0):=0h(0):=0; then M:=max[0,1]⁡hM:=\max_{[0,1]}h is finite and attained at an interior ϕ∗\phi^{*}, and with c0:=r/Mc_{0}:=r/M: (a) for c<c0c<c_{0} the only fixed point in [0,1][0,1] is ϕ=0\phi=0, and it is asymptotically stable — the circuit direction has no resting place at all; (b) for c>c0c>c_{0} at least two positive fixed points ϕ−<ϕ+\phi_{-}<\phi_{+} exist, ϕ−\phi_{-} unstable and ϕ+\phi_{+} stable — metastability with activated crossing over ϕ−\phi_{-}; (c) if G∈C1G\in C^{1} and ϕ∗\phi^{*} is a non-degenerate maximum of hh, the pair is born at c=c0c=c_{0} through a tangency: a saddle–node (fold), not a transcritical exchange.

Proof.

The three properties are consequences of results already established. (D1) is the replicator geometry of softmax attention plus the restoring-force computation: the exact identity ∂𝔼⁡[L]/∂sj=aj​(ℓj−⟨ℓ⟩a)\partial\mathbb{E}[L]/\partial s_{j}=a_{j}(\ell_{j}-\langle\ell\rangle_{a}) (Lemma 8) makes every drift on an attention mass proportional to that mass, and the competitor supplies a per-unit-mass restoring force bounded below by λ′>0\lambda^{\prime}>0 uniformly over the basin (Lemma 7), weighted by its stream share 1−c1-c. A product of KK masses each decaying at rate (1−c)​λ′(1-c)\lambda^{\prime} decays at K⁡(1−c)​λ′K(1-c)\lambda^{\prime}, so linearity survives the product. Linear decay is thus forced by the simplex geometry, not chosen for convenience. (D2) is no-partial-credit in dynamical form, and the two structures compose. By Lemma 4 the target’s pull per unit mass at a required slot rr is controlled by the product over the other required slots, ϕ/Ar\phi/A_{r}; the replicator factor of (D1) then gives A˙r∝Ar⋅(ϕ/Ar)=ϕ\dot{A}_{r}\propto A_{r}\cdot(\phi/A_{r})=\phi, and ϕ˙=ϕ​∑rA˙r/Ar\dot{\phi}=\phi\sum_{r}\dot{A}_{r}/A_{r} yields, in the symmetric configuration Ar=ϕ1/KA_{r}=\phi^{1/K},

G⁡(ϕ)∝K​ϕ 2−1/K,G(\phi)\;\propto\;K\,\phi^{\,2-1/K},

whose exponent exceeds 11 for every K≥2K\geq 2, so G⁡(ϕ)/ϕ→0G(\phi)/\phi\to 0. A term linear in ϕ\phi would be precisely partial credit, which Lemma 1 excludes exactly; note also that the exponent rises with KK, so deeper conjunctions have flatter origins and, by the argument below, higher floors. (D3) is the cross-entropy’s own saturation together with the simplex bound: masses lie in [0,1][0,1], so GG is bounded; and when every part is in place the model predicts the target correctly, the error probability 1−pc→01-p_{c}\to 0, and with it the label-dependent gradient — G⁡(1)=0G(1)=0. Nothing is imposed by hand: the gain rises out of the origin, is capped by the simplex, and is switched off by being right. The conclusion follows. hh is continuous on the compact [0,1][0,1] (continuity at 00 is (D2), at 11 it is 00 by (D3)), hence attains a finite maximum MM at some ϕ∗\phi^{*}, interior because h>0h>0 on (0,1)(0,1) and h⁡(0)=h⁡(1)=0h(0)=h(1)=0. Positive fixed points solve c​h​(ϕ)=rc\,h(\phi)=r. (a) If c<c0c<c_{0} then c​h​(ϕ)≤c​M<rc\,h(\phi)\leq cM<r everywhere, so no positive root; and near the origin ϕ˙=ϕ⁡(c​h​(ϕ)−r)<0\dot{\phi}=\phi(c\,h(\phi)-r)<0, giving asymptotic stability of ϕ=0\phi=0. (b) If c>c0c>c_{0} then c​h​(ϕ∗)>rc\,h(\phi^{*})>r while c​h​(0)=c​h​(1)=0<rc\,h(0)=c\,h(1)=0<r, so the intermediate value theorem gives a root on each side of ϕ∗\phi^{*}; the sign of ϕ˙=ϕ⁡(c​h−r)\dot{\phi}=\phi(ch-r) changes −,+,−-,+,- across them, which is exactly ϕ−\phi_{-} unstable, ϕ+\phi_{+} stable. (c) At c=c0c=c_{0} the equation c​h=rc\,h=r holds only at ϕ∗\phi^{*}, where h′​(ϕ∗)=0h^{\prime}(\phi^{*})=0: the curves are tangent, and non-degeneracy (h′′​(ϕ∗)<0h^{\prime\prime}(\phi^{*})<0) gives the standard saddle–node normal form, so the two branches are born together rather than crossing. ∎

Remark 6.

Earlier versions of this argument assumed a reduced drift −r​ϕ+c​g​ϕm/(1+ϕm)-r\phi+cg\,\phi^{m}/(1+\phi^{m}) and flagged the linear decay and the saturating form as modeling choices. They are choices no longer. (D1) is the replicator geometry of the softmax — every drift on an attention mass is proportional to that mass, exactly (Lemma 8) — combined with a restoring force per unit mass that is bounded below uniformly in the basin (Lemma 7); (D2) is Lemma 1 in dynamical form, a linear term being precisely the partial credit the task class excludes; (D3) is the simplex bound plus the fact that a model which is right receives no gradient. Nothing about the shape of GG between its two zeros is used — no functional form is assumed at all — which also means the floor’s existence cannot be an artifact of the algebra chosen to express it. What the derivation costs, stated plainly: Lemma 8 is general to softmax attention, but Lemmas 7 and 4 are proved inside the controlled gated-attention model of App. A, so (D1)–(D2) inherit that model’s idealizations (positional attention, readout locality, oracle gating). The gain is therefore not that the floor has become assumption-free — it is that the assumptions have moved from a chosen formula to a stated model, where each is a consequence of an established lemma and each carries its own measurement. A reader who rejects the gated model may still read Prop. 3 as before, taking (D1)–(D3) as three structural hypotheses; that is strictly weaker than the previous version, which additionally fixed the functional form. Each ingredient additionally has its own measurement: a floor appears only against a persistent competitor (the three-diluent sweep below: inert and quickly-mastered fillers give no floor, so a fixed r>0r>0 is the operative condition), and the reinforcement demonstrably does not run away but balances at finite ϕ\phi (below c0c_{0} formed circuits dissolve to chance within 200 steps; above it they survive 8/88/8). The model also predicts the phenomenology above the floor: bistability with activated crossing — the memoryless waiting measured in EK-1 — and a barrier that shrinks with drive — the throttle. The floor hypothesis of the next proposition is thereby derived, not free-standing.

Proposition 4 (Intensivity and the effective floor (suppression beyond nucleation order)).

Suppose (i) the drive enters the generation term of Eq. (1) only through the per-step concentration cc of capability-relevant statistics (an intensive quantity), and (ii) for c<c0c<c_{0} the circuit configuration is not metastable under the drift: it is disjoint from the attractor set, the destruction drift exceeding the generation drift along every formation path. Then: (a) (intensivity) at fixed c<c0c<c_{0}, increasing total tokens, steps, or batch size cannot induce formation — the floor is independent of budget; (b) (beyond-order suppression) the per-attempt probability of a sustained crossing (ϕ>1/2\phi>1/2 held for a window τ\tau) is bounded by e−aτ/εe^{-a\tau/\varepsilon} for some a>0a>0, so formation is suppressed beyond any nucleation-rate order: unlike escape into a metastable target, which is a one-shot barrier crossing, holding an unstable configuration costs action linearly in the holding time. (We do not claim a strictly zero probability for a stochastic process; the claim is the qualitative separation between one-shot barrier crossing above the floor and time-extensive holding cost below it — and hypothesis (ii) is not circular bookkeeping but the floor’s measured content: sub-critical embryos are directly observed stalling and dissolving below c0c_{0}.)

Proof.

(a) Under (i), the token budget enters only as the number of attempts nn; the per-attempt success probability p⁡(c)p(c) depends on cc alone. If p⁡(c)=0p(c)=0 then 1−(1−p⁡(c))n=01-(1-p(c))^{n}=0 for every nn; more generally, by (b), p(c)≤e−aτ/εp(c)\leq e^{-a\tau/\varepsilon} uniformly in nn, so any subexponential budget leaves the total probability vanishing as ε→0\varepsilon\to 0. (b) By hypothesis (ii) the set {ϕ>1/2}\{\phi>1/2\} contains no attractor of the drift for c<c0c<c_{0}. By the Freidlin–Wentzell estimates for occupation of neighborhoods of non-attracting compact sets [26, Ch. 4], a trajectory that remains in such a neighborhood for time τ\tau must follow a path whose action grows at least linearly in τ\tau — there is a per-unit-time cost a>0a>0 to hold the state against the drift — whence the probability bound e−aτ/εe^{-a\tau/\varepsilon}. (We use only the sojourn estimate, not the full exit theory. The drift hypothesis is no longer free-standing: Proposition 3 derives it from no-partial-credit plus saturation, and it is independently the measured content of the floor — sub-critical embryos are directly observed stalling and dissolving below c0c_{0}.) ∎

The measured floor matches both clauses. Intensivity: a 4×44\times 4 concentration×\timesbatch grid (Fig. 6) shows c=0.20c=0.20 never igniting at any batch (b64 = 8×\times the tokens of b8) while c≥0.35c\geq 0.35 always ignites; a finer sweep locates the 70M floor sharply (0/12 for c≤0.26c\leq 0.26; 4/5 at c=0.28c=0.28). Beyond-order suppression (not mere slowness): the near-floor divergence τ∝(c−c0)−γ\tau\propto(c-c_{0})^{-\gamma}, γ=0.62±0.01\gamma=0.62\pm 0.01 (R2R^{2} 0.999), with sub-critical embryos observed stalling and dissolving below the floor — the driving-force law of nucleation, not a capacity story. The floor is intensive but not scale-invariant: it falls 0.27→0.20→∼0.170.27\to 0.20\to{\sim}0.17 from 70M to 410M, consistent with a weak power law, c0≈0.26​(N/70​M)−0.26c_{0}\approx 0.26\,(N/70\mathrm{M})^{-0.26} (R2=0.96R^{2}=0.96 on three points — reported as the measured trend and an extrapolation hypothesis, not an established law, since three points cannot fix an exponent). Within the igniting region, batch enters as b−0.33±0.05b^{-0.33\pm 0.05} and learning rate only accelerates: at fixed mix, lr and batch are clocks; the mix is the drive. Above the floor the throttle is steep: never / ∼\sim1,400 / ∼\sim470 steps at doses 0.15/0.30/0.50 (Fig. 7).

What “concentration” has to mean: three diluents, one apparatus. The real-model floor leaves a definitional question open — concentration of what, measured against what? We settled it in the shortcut-free apparatus by holding the target task, the model, and the optimizer fixed and changing only the material the target is diluted into, sweeping the target’s share over up to 33×33\times in each case. Inert diluent (uniform random tokens): formation time is flat — log–log slope 00 over an 8×8\times density change, no floor. The inertness is the point: unpredictable filler contributes no gradient, so the target’s share of the gradient never changes however its share of the tokens falls; and a pure gain change is in any case normalized away by AdamW’s per-parameter scaling. Saturating diluent (a single competing copy skill): slope −0.22-0.22, still no floor, and at intermediate dilution formation is faster than at full strength — the competitor is learned within ∼\sim100 steps, after which it stops competing, and the offset-selective head it built seeds the target (the cross-nucleation effect of Dong [25], reproduced unbidden). Non-saturating diluent (a family of 24>H24>H copy skills, so the background always has something left to learn): the slope steepens past the product law and diverges (−0.55→−1.67-0.55\to-1.67), and a floor appears. The lesson is a definition: supersaturation is the target’s share of the gradient against a persistent competitor, not its share of the token stream — which is exactly why natural text, never exhausted, produces a floor in real models while an inert or quickly-mastered filler cannot.

The floor is a stability threshold, not an absence of events. Pushing the target share down in the non-saturating apparatus, formation events do not simply stop: at 0.5%0.5\% the waiting times split into two clusters (3.83.8–6.96.9k versus 8383–159159k steps), one seed forms and then dissolves, and one is censored at 2×1052\times 10^{5} steps — a flickering band, the signature of net rate crossing zero rather than of a hard kinetic wall. Measuring the destruction side directly resolves it. Seeding the circuit at c=0.25c=0.25 and then switching the stream to a maintenance concentration choldc_{\rm hold} gives survival 8/88/8, 8/88/8, 8/88/8, 5/85/8, 2/82/8, 0/80/8 at chold=0.25,0.06,0.02,0.005,0.001,0c_{\rm hold}=0.25,0.06,0.02,0.005,0.001,0 (30k held-out steps; 2%2\% vs 0.1%0.1\% Fisher p=0.007p=0.007, vs 00 p=1.6×10−4p=1.6\times 10^{-4}), with the un-reduced arm surviving 8/88/8 — so the collapse is caused by the concentration drop, not by continued training. At zero drive a formed circuit dissolves to chance within 200 steps. The two measurements agree on where the floor sits (0.10.1–0.5%0.5\%), and together they say something sharper than the proposition assumed: below the floor the capability is not merely never built, it cannot be held — Proposition 3’s “no resting place” read as an experiment. The two protocols are not identical, and this yields a prediction for real models: below their floor, budgets far longer than ours should show transient, flickering formation rather than a blank, since our 0/120/12 was measured at a fixed budget.

The switch, including from scratch. Ignition follows an experimenter-chosen switch of the data mix past the floor 10/10; without it, never. From random initialization — no pretrained substrate — the same three laws reproduce: plain data never ignites (0.02–0.03 through 16k steps); the switch ignites 2/2 (∼\sim700 steps); a delayed switch pays a growing tax; switching too late never ignites (Fig. 8; the tax and deadline belong to the backward reading, §7). Cross-family, on OLMo-1B: control 0/2 never, switch 2/2 at ∼\sim247, delayed switch taxed (τ\tau 471/799).

7 Reading the equation backward: loss of plasticity

Backward means: hold the drive available but let training itself consume the site term NN. The equation then predicts a specific, testable structure for how learnability dies — and a discriminator separating it from every drive-side explanation.

Proposition 5 (Site-limited versus drive-limited failure, and the horizon).

In Eq. (1) with factorized generation G=N​ν​σ​(c)​e−β​KG=N\nu\,\sigma(c)\,e^{-\beta K}: (a) ∂G/∂c=N​ν​σ′​(c)​e−β​K>0\partial G/\partial c=N\nu\,\sigma^{\prime}(c)\,e^{-\beta K}>0 whenever N>0N>0 and σ′>0\sigma^{\prime}>0, while if N=0N=0 then G=0G=0 for every cc. Hence raising the drive rescues a drive-limited substrate and cannot rescue a site-limited one: the response to a drive increase is a discriminating experiment between the two failure modes. (b) Let Nmin​(c):=D/(ν​σ​(c)​e−β​K)N_{\min}(c):=D/(\nu\,\sigma(c)\,e^{-\beta K}) be the fewest sites at which generation clears destruction at drive cc; it is decreasing in cc. If the site count decays with occupation time SS (training on other data) as a non-increasing N⁡(S)N(S), the plasticity horizon at drive cc is tc​(c)=inf{S:N⁡(S)<Nmin​(c)}t_{c}(c)=\inf\{S:N(S)<N_{\min}(c)\}, non-decreasing in cc. Past tc​(c)t_{c}(c), formation is impossible at that drive, and possible again only by one of exactly two routes: re-opening sites (raising NN), or raising the drive past the escape threshold cesc​(S):=inf{c:Nmin​(c)≤N⁡(S)}c_{\rm esc}(S):=\inf\{c:N_{\min}(c)\leq N(S)\} — the drive at which generation on the residual sites clears destruction again.

Proof.

(a) is immediate from the factorized form (itself the mean-field structure whose validity domain is measured in §9): cc enters only through σ⁡(c)\sigma(c), multiplied by NN. (b) Nmin​(c)N_{\min}(c) is decreasing because σ\sigma is increasing; hence tc​(c)t_{c}(c) is non-decreasing. For S>tc​(c)S>t_{c}(c), N​(S)<Nmin​(c)N(S)<N_{\min}(c) gives G=N⁡(S)​ν​σ​(c)​e−β​K<DG=N(S)\nu\sigma(c)e^{-\beta K}<D: net rate negative, ϕ\phi cannot cross. The net rate is restored exactly by raising NN above Nmin​(c)N_{\min}(c) or by raising cc until Nmin​(c)≤N⁡(S)N_{\min}(c)\leq N(S), i.e. c≥cesc​(S)c\geq c_{\rm esc}(S); monotonicity of NminN_{\min} makes cescc_{\rm esc} a sharp threshold. ∎

Site dynamics, closing the loop. The forward reading has a rate law; symmetry demands the backward reading have one too, not an exogenous “NN decreases.” The closure is

d​Nd​S=−λ⁡(θ⁡(S))​N+R,\frac{dN}{dS}\;=\;-\,\lambda(\theta(S))\,N\;+\;R,

where λ\lambda is the occupation rate — mechanistically identified below as attention-subspace commitment — and RR is site re-opening, zero in native training and exogenously actuated by our reset and graft interventions (they are the RR term, performed by hand). We deliberately do not impose a parametric form for λ\lambda: with the occupancy protocol run at zero target drive (c=0c=0 during aging, so the depletion measured here is occupation by the base task alone, not consumption by target-crystal growth — the coupled case is outside this protocol and stated as such), the equation integrates to N(S)/N(0)=e−∫0SλN(S)/N(0)=e^{-\int_{0}^{S}\lambda}, and since formation time scales as 1/N1/N at fixed drive (Prop. 5), the measured, non-parametric depletion curve is N⁡(S)/N⁡(0)=τ⁡(0)/τ⁡(S)N(S)/N(0)=\tau(0)/\tau(S): 1→0.46→0.451\to 0.46\to 0.45 at S=0/600/1200S=0/600/1200, crossing Nmin​(c=0.5)N_{\min}(c{=}0.5) before S=3600S=3600. Three points and a bound do not fix a functional form, and we decline to overfit one; what they do fix is the structure — depletion is real, monotone, drive-independent in this protocol, mechanistically located (λ\lambda tracks commitment at r=0.93r=0.93), and reversible only through the RR term. The scale law enters as d​λ/d⁡(size)<0d\lambda/d(\text{size})<0 (aging slope 0.69→0.160.69\to 0.16 from 70M to 410M).

The proposition’s content is that these are measurable alternatives, and every measurement lands on the site side. The discriminator: on a substrate aged past its horizon, doubling the drive does not rescue (0/3), while opening new sites does — grafted fresh head pairs ignite with lightning kinetics (200–500 steps) at per-pair success p≈0.15p\approx 0.15 consistent with independent-site statistics, and sites must be opened in pairs across both layers (single-layer openings: 0/6), exactly as a two-layer composition requires. Learnability death is a site-term failure, not a drive-term failure. The tax and the horizon: the post-switch delay grows with waiting (n=5n=5 seeds: τ=506±44→1108±66→1115±65\tau=506\pm 44\to 1108\pm 66\to 1115\pm 65 at S=0/600/1200S=0/600/1200); at S=3600S=3600 no ignition in 4,400 further steps (tail slope zero — not censoring). The horizon has a scale law: tc≈3200t_{c}\approx 3200 (70M), >6000>6000 (160M), >8000>8000 (410M); the aging slope falls 0.69→0.160.69\to 0.16 — larger substrates age slower (Fig. 9). Drive-relative death: the dead substrate revives above a sharp escape drive — 0/2 at 0.60–0.69, 2/3 at 0.71, 2/2 at ≥\geq0.72; threshold cesc=0.705±0.005c_{\rm esc}=0.705\pm 0.005 — clause (b)’s second route, observed, including its predicted sharpness (monotone NminN_{\min} makes cescc_{\rm esc} a threshold, not a gradient). The located mechanism: during waiting, every head’s attention pattern grows more committed (peakedness +45%+45\%, entropy −20%-20\%), tracking the tax at r=0.93r=0.93. What ages is recruitable capacity, not the existing parts: the precursor head itself keeps growing throughout the waiting period, and what is exhausted is the supply of uncommitted heads — which is why the failure is site-limited (above) and why it is repaired by re-opening sites rather than by rebuilding parts. Targeted resets make this causal — restoring only the attention weights of a dead model rescues ignition 5/5 (vs. 0/5 un-reset controls), restoring MLP rescues weakly, restoring embeddings does not (0/2), replicating at 160M and 410M. The two reset arms separate with non-overlapping Wilson 95% intervals (5/55/5: [0.57,1.00][0.57,1.00]; 0/50/5: [0.00,0.43][0.00,0.43]; Fisher exact p=0.008p=0.008), as do the floor arms (0/120/12 below the floor: [0.00,0.24][0.00,0.24]; 4/54/5 above it: [0.38,0.96][0.38,0.96]). The active ingredient, isolated. Theorem 1(iii) says occupation lives in the attention pattern, so the score channel should carry the entire cure and the value channel none of it; the apparatus confirmed this (App. A.7), and the prediction was then tested on the real substrate by slicing the fused QKV projection head-wise. It separates completely (six seeds, one aged substrate per seed, all four arms run from it): un-reset 0/60/6; re-initializing only the query–key slices 6/66/6 (Fisher p=0.002p=0.002 against control); re-initializing only the value slices and the output projection 0/60/6 — indistinguishable from doing nothing (induction score 0.2520.252 vs 0.2630.263 un-reset, against 0.7000.700 for the QK arm); and the whole-block reset 6/66/6, exactly equal to the QK arm. The block reset’s entire therapeutic effect comes from the score channel. This converts the repair from a coarse intervention into a prescription — reset QK, keep OV — and supplies the sharpest causal evidence in the paper that what ages is attention allocation rather than the content the heads carry. (Note the distinction: this reset re-opens sites for a capability that has never formed on this substrate; it does not act on formed structure. The melt hierarchy of §8, in which formed compositions dissolve before their parts, is a different axis — destruction of what exists versus recovery of the ability to build — and the two results are consistent, not in tension.) Loss-blindness: throughout the aging that kills inducibility, validation loss falls smoothly (5.46→1.635.46\to 1.63) — standard monitoring is structurally blind to the site term, which is why the phenomenon has stayed invisible to ordinary telemetry (Fig. 10).

7.1 The deadline as a theorem: occupation in a controlled gated-attention model

Everything above is measured. This subsection reports that the site story is also provable — as a theorem in a controlled model — with a division of labor that deserves emphasis: the deadline’s consequences (irrecoverability by data, repair by reset, invisibility in the loss) require no ergodicity assumption at all. Confinement is the easy direction of stochastic analysis — a drift inequality plus bounded increments (Hajek’s drift theorem [38]) — in contrast to the rate law’s upper-bound side, which carries Assumption 1. The paper’s backward reading thus stands on the unconditional side of the mathematics.

The model (full detail in App. A): HH position-attention heads (softmax scores over WW window offsets); a data stream mixing background skills (cue token gi→g_{i}\to copy the token at offset oio_{i}; traffic share πi\pi_{i}), target queries (share cc; the KK-slot no-partial-credit task of Lemma 1), and neutral substrate; a readout gated by the current token, with the substrate channel closed. The gate is the model’s most idealized ingredient — it hands the model an oracle task identity. The point of retaining it is sharp: in this model the difficulty of late learning is provably pure capacity occupation — even knowing exactly which task is which, a substrate short of KK uncommitted heads cannot form the capability. Each structural assumption has the empirical counterpart measured above (commitment at r=0.93r=0.93; control ablations retaining 99% — the readout does approximate “read only the carrier”; reset 5/5), which licenses the abstraction without claiming it as a theorem.

Theorem 1 (Occupation: the silent deadline, in the gated model).

Under assumptions (G1)–(G8) and feasibility/scale conditions C0–C4 of App. A, with formation requiring KK heads on distinct target slots: (i) (deadline; uses the recruitment assumption) the number of uncommitted-or-loosely-pinned heads is non-increasing with high probability over the recruitment window, and the deadline tdeadt_{\rm dead} (fewer than KK such heads) is a.s. finite, with 𝔼⁡[tdead]≲(H−K+1)/(ρmin​p0)\mathbb{E}[t_{\rm dead}]\lesssim(H-K+1)/(\rho_{\min}p_{0}). We do not claim a constant per-head recruitment hazard: the traffic-share structure of C0 (μi∝πi\mu_{i}\propto\pi_{i}) implies the opposite, and we measure it below. (ii) (data cannot rescue; no mixing) past tdeadt_{\rm dead}, P⁡(formation within ​T​ steps)≤H​K​T​e−θ​ΔP(\text{formation within }T\text{ steps})\leq HKT\,e^{-\theta\Delta} with θ=Ω⁡(μ/(η​G2))\theta=\Omega\!\big(\mu/(\eta G^{2})\big); the target share cc enters μ\mu only linearly, so rescue by data requires cc large enough to break the background’s own pinning margin — the catastrophic-forgetting dual, not a gentle scaling. (iii) (reset rescues; no mixing) re-initializing the attention scores of any KK heads restores the fresh-substrate formation rate. (iv) (silence; no mixing) pre-formation the target loss equals ln⁡V\ln V plus a bounded junk term held near zero, and the background loss decreases through tdeadt_{\rm dead} in steps of the same order at every pinning event: the deadline produces no discontinuity, kink, or necessary precursor in any loss-derived scalar. The step that kills learnability looks, in the loss, like every other step of ordinary background learning.

Proof chain (full proofs in App. A): pre-formation, the target exerts on any single head only a pull proportional to a product of attention masses on the required slots — an iterated-oscillation bound on full-support Fourier coefficients, valid because the readout sees window contents only through head outputs — together with an exact decomposition of the cross-entropy gradient into a uniformizing potential (label-free) and a signal covariance; the attention simplex makes carried and target patterns exclusive; a linear-response computation, every block carrying the (1−pc)(1-p_{c}) factor, gives a restoring drift toward the carried offset; an exact score-difference identity turns the force ledger into a drift inequality; Hajek’s theorem converts drift into exponential confinement with no ergodicity input; and stochastic domination of the recruitment process yields the deadline.

The theorem’s predictions, tested — including one we had to withdraw. We ran the theorem’s own falsifiable consequences in the apparatus (App. A.7). Confirmed, and sharper than the real-model result that motivated it: the repair is specific to the attention score channel. From one aged substrate, re-initializing the QK slices recovers formation 4.3×\times (6/6 formed), MLP does little (0.81×0.81\times), and re-initializing the OV slices is worse than no reset at all (1.76×1.76\times slower) — occupation lives in the attention pattern, so freeing the pattern is the repair, while resetting the value channel destroys learned structure and frees nothing. This turns §7’s block reset (5/5 vs 0/5) into a prescription — reset QK, keep OV — which we then confirmed prospectively on the real substrate: on aged Pythia-70M the QK arm ignites 6/6, the OV arm 0/6 (identical to no reset), and the block reset 6/6, i.e. exactly the QK arm and nothing more (§7). Falsified: we had additionally assumed a constant per-head recruitment hazard, which would make occupation decay exponentially and the deadline scale as log⁡H\log H. It does not: the hazard falls ≈\approx15×\times across the sweep (32→18→8→532\to 18\to 8\to 5 available slots), and extrapolating the initial rate misses by ∼\sim1500×\times. The failed clause was an extra simplification that contradicted our own traffic-share model — with pull μi∝πi\mu_{i}\propto\pi_{i}, high-traffic skills take heads first and the remainder recruit slowly, so the hazard must decline. We withdraw the clause and the log⁡H\log H prediction with it; the mechanism, the finiteness of the deadline, and clauses (ii)–(iv) are untouched. The correction also resolves a tension we had flagged: Pythia’s saturating depletion profile (1→0.46→0.451\to 0.46\to 0.45) is the same declining-hazard family, not a counterexample.

Position in the plasticity literature. The phenomenon is established [7, 8], the remedies are empirical [39], and the causes literature is explicitly partial — no single proposed mechanism suffices [9]. Lyle et al. [40] conjecture, via effective learning rate, that the dynamics of emergence and of plasticity loss are linked; we cite that as the conceptual precursor and supply the quantitative form the conjecture lacks: the same rate equation whose forward reading is §6, with a law (τ⁡(S)\tau(S)), a horizon (tct_{c} and its scale law), a located and causally verified mechanism (attention-subspace commitment), a repair (targeted reset), and a discriminator (drive versus sites) that rules out the drive-side alternatives. Theorem 1 adds the tier the causes literature is missing: a proof, in a controlled model, that occupation must produce exactly this phenomenology — deadline, data-irrecoverability, reset-repair, and silence.

8 Completing the equation: injected temperature and process control

The knockdown component of DD in Eq. (1) is dormant in native training (§5: nothing qualifies as a temperature, and at practical learning rates weight drift, not noise, is the only destroyer of formed structure). Installing the missing term — an isotropic weight-noise bath of magnitude TT, a few lines of code — completes the equation and turns it into a control surface.
