Everything in this section is measured in a controlled apparatus (a conjunction-circuit toy with K=2..4K=2..4, plus real-Pythia induction circuits), with constants frozen and out-of-sample tests preregistered.

Why inject a temperature at all?

Since emergence needs no bath (§6: the drive is data), one may ask whether this section adds anything data cannot. It adds exactly the operations that a monotone drive cannot express. Data can only push formation forward, in barrier order; it cannot pause a capability below threshold and release it on command (pinning at ϕs​s\phi_{ss}), cannot selectively erase one circuit while sparing its parts (the melt line — the primitive machine unlearning lacks), and cannot accelerate a high-barrier circuit past its own kinetics (the nose, where annealing beats a gradient-filter baseline). The bath is also the theory’s instrument: melt points, the hysteresis window, dose–damage bookkeeping, and ϕs​s​(T)\phi_{ss}(T) are measurements of the destruction term and of basin depths that native training simply cannot perform — no thermometer, no thermometry. We therefore present these schedules as existence proofs that every term of Eq. (1) is independently actuatable — the completion of the program — and as measurement instruments, not as a claim that production training should run with a bath on.

8.1 The nose: barrier-gated annealing

With a qualified temperature, generation gains a barrier-assistance factor (crossing aided by total noise ε0+T\varepsilon_{0}+T) while destruction turns on above a damage onset. These two monotonicities force the shape of the formation-time curve:

Proposition 6 (Existence of a TTT nose, if and only if barrier-gated).

Let the generation rate g⁡(T)g(T) be continuous and strictly increasing in TT (barrier assistance), and the destruction rate d⁡(T)d(T) be continuous, non-decreasing, d≡0d\equiv 0 on [0,Tdam][0,T_{\rm dam}] for some damage onset Tdam>0T_{\rm dam}>0, with g⁡(Tceil)=d⁡(Tceil)g(T_{\rm ceil})=d(T_{\rm ceil}) at some finite ceiling Tceil>TdamT_{\rm ceil}>T_{\rm dam}. Define the formation time τ⁡(T)=C/(g⁡(T)−d⁡(T))\tau(T)=C/(g(T)-d(T)) on [0,Tceil)[0,T_{\rm ceil}). Then: (a) τ\tau is strictly decreasing on [0,Tdam][0,T_{\rm dam}] and τ⁡(T)→∞\tau(T)\to\infty as T→Tceil−T\to T_{\rm ceil}^{-}; hence τ\tau attains an interior minimum (a nose) in [Tdam,Tceil)[T_{\rm dam},T_{\rm ceil}). (b) If instead the barrier is negligible — gg constant in TT — then τ\tau is non-decreasing on all of [0,Tceil)[0,T_{\rm ceil}) and the minimum is at T=0T=0: cold is fastest, and no nose exists. Thus an interior nose exists precisely when there is a barrier for temperature to assist.

Proof.

(a) On [0,Tdam][0,T_{\rm dam}], d=0d=0 and gg is strictly increasing, so τ=C/g\tau=C/g is strictly decreasing there; and g−d→0+g-d\to 0^{+} as T→Tceil−T\to T_{\rm ceil}^{-}, so τ→∞\tau\to\infty. Since τ\tau is continuous on [Tdam,Tceil)[T_{\rm dam},T_{\rm ceil}) and diverges at the right end, it attains a minimum on that interval at some finite T∗T^{*}; by the strict decrease on [0,Tdam][0,T_{\rm dam}], T∗T^{*} is the global minimizer over [0,Tceil)[0,T_{\rm ceil}) and satisfies Tdam≤T∗<TceilT_{\rm dam}\leq T^{*}<T_{\rm ceil} — an interior point of the temperature domain, i.e. a nose. (b) With gg constant, g−dg-d is non-increasing, so τ\tau is non-decreasing; the minimum is at T=0T=0. ∎

The measured curves realize both branches exactly as the proposition sorts them: K=2K=2 (barrier assist capped at 1.11×1.11\times) shows no nose in six curves — cold fastest, the (b) branch; K=3K=3 (assist 2.17×2.17\times) shows a clean nose at T≈0.003T\approx 0.003, non-overlapping across seeds, depth 23–41%; K=4K=4 confirms. The full C-curve formula (attempt ×\times assistance ×\times ceiling proximity), with constants frozen on-axis, predicts a held-out drive lane at median 13.9% error and a prospective double-nose position hit at 14.3% — and yields the intrinsic noise scale of SGD itself, ε0≈5×10−4\varepsilon_{0}\approx 5\times 10^{-4}, as a fit constant (the quantitative version of “the cold arm does not freeze”). As an application, nose-temperature annealing accelerates a chosen high-barrier circuit ∼\sim2×\times over the Grokfast baseline [41] — a mechanism-guided schedule versus a gradient filter. And the construction is a genuine TTT diagram, not only a formation-time curve: post-nucleation growth follows Johnson–Mehl–Avrami–Kolmogorov kinetics with measured Avrami exponent n≈1.16n\approx 1.16 (single-front growth) [42, 25], supplying the transformed-fraction axis X⁡(t,T)X(t,T) that the metallurgical analogy requires.

8.2 The melt line: destruction is a weakest-link law

Formation and destruction read the same part count KK through opposite logical gates, and this duality is provable.

Proposition 7 (Weakest-link melting, and the build/break duality).

Let a circuit function if and only if all KK of its links function (the defining conjunction), and let link ii fail when the perturbation exceeds a threshold σi\sigma_{i}. Then: (a) the circuit’s melt threshold is σ∗=mini⁡σi\sigma^{*}=\min_{i}\sigma_{i}: it fails as soon as any link fails; (b) for nested circuits S⊂S′S\subset S^{\prime}, σ∗​(S′)≤σ∗​(S)\sigma^{*}(S^{\prime})\leq\sigma^{*}(S): composition depth can only lower, never raise, the melt point; (c) (duality) over the same part set, the formation cost is a sum (Prop. 1: all parts must co-occur — an AND for building) while the destruction threshold is a min (any part’s failure suffices — an OR for breaking). Compositional circuits are therefore simultaneously hard to build and easy to break, with both facts derived from the same KK.

Proof.

(a) Failure of the circuit is the union ⋃i{link ​i​ fails}\bigcup_{i}\{\text{link }i\text{ fails}\}, which first occurs at perturbation mini⁡σi\min_{i}\sigma_{i}. (b) The minimum over a superset is at most the minimum over the subset. (c) is (a) juxtaposed with Prop. 1: the intersection event prices formation as a sum of exponents; the union event prices destruction as a minimum of thresholds. ∎

Measured, at circuit grain and across scale: melt thresholds under injected weight noise order parts ≫\gg compositions in 20/21 model–pair tests across both families (2.5–6×\times; one 8% local inversion reported as such; Fig. 11); on real Pythia the previous-token head melts at 5.3–6.4×\times the induction head’s threshold at every scale — both are near scale-invariant material constants (induction: 0.0017–0.0025 across 31M–410M synthetic; 0.00028–0.00063 real-text), and their ratio is a constant of the composition. The parts survive to perturbations where the composition’s inter-layer wiring has long failed — the weakest link is the composition itself, clause (b) in the wild. Melting is first-order-like (cliff, not slope), sits above the formation ceiling (a hysteresis window, measured (0.03, 0.05) in the toy), and melt points scale with maintenance strength (3–8×\times between data regimes) — a dynamic, driven melting point, as the non-equilibrium branch requires. Applications: selective dissolution — at T=0.001T=0.001, induction dies while the previous-token part survives, demonstrated on real Pythia at three scales; and a risk rule for practitioners — assess a model’s fragility by its longest chain, not its parts.

8.3 Glass, quench, and the release protocol

Between the nose and the melt line lies the third control primitive: pinning. Holding a bath at window temperature pins every sub-threshold structure at a steady-state order parameter ϕs​s​(T)\phi_{ss}(T) — measured as a clean decreasing spectrum (0.373/0.303/0.204/0.164/0.1060.373/0.303/0.204/0.164/0.106 at T=0.003..0.02T=0.003..0.02, seed spread ±0.02\pm 0.02) with ∼\sim100×\times retardation of ordering, the driven-steady-state picture of irradiated alloys [43]. Release is not merely removing the bath: on real text, pure-temperature release fails (0/16) because quenching freezes the disorder in — the burned state has weights inflated 5–24×\times and attention entropy collapsed to saturation. The working protocol is quench plus mechanism surgery: rescaling attention-weight RMS to healthy values at release (direction preserved) recovers 6/6, and attention-only surgery re-ignites in ∼\sim500 steps — faster than a virgin substrate, the held heat converted into a head start. Damage bookkeeping is a dose law: below the knockdown line, zero accumulated damage; above it, damage ∝\propto knockdown rate ×\times duration (R2R^{2} 0.952) — discrete Poisson-avalanche knockdowns, not diffusive wear, consistent with the jump-type destruction term.

The control palette, then: seeds and sites choose which (a transplanted sub-critical seed re-orders barriers — the only lawful way to invert the temperature-forced order, 8/8); drive chooses whether and how fast (floor and throttle); temperature chooses when (pin at ϕs​s\phi_{ss}, release by quench-plus-surgery); the melt line chooses what survives. Each primitive is a term of Eq. (1).

9 The engine, the synthesis, and the boundary

Two duties remain to the spine: measuring the equation’s one non-obvious input (KK, the part count), and testing its structure (the factorization) where all axes move at once.

The engine. Given only a behavioral probe, single-head ablation at a just-post-ignition checkpoint returns the circuit’s constituent parts; tracking each constituent’s attention-pattern crystallinity across checkpoints reveals which arrived first — that part is the precursor, and its count is KK (Fig. 12). Blind runs recover the known circuits in 10/11 capability–scale pairs. The count is physically load-bearing, not descriptive: induction (K=2K=2, C=1.24C=1.24) and IOI away from the wall (K=4K=4, C=2.1C=2.1) share β≈0.23\beta\approx 0.23, whereas the textbook depth assignment (K=3K=3 for IOI) is inconsistent with the clock — the machine count is the one the physics accepts. Nor is the count circular: KK is measured by ablation at a single checkpoint, with no access to formation times, and only then inserted into the clock — an independently measured input that could have failed to unify the constants (the textbook K=3K{=}3 does fail), not a parameter tuned to make them agree.

The count’s domain of validity, measured. We delimited it directly, by sweeping single-head ablation of the copy capability across four scales and two checkpoints (behavioural probe; chance ≈0\approx 0). Two facts emerge, and the second is a real limitation. First, the count is right where the theory uses it: at a just-post-ignition checkpoint in the smallest model the individually-necessary set is exactly {\{previous-token head, induction head}\} — K=2K=2, both known parts recovered by a criterion that had no access to their identity — and at 160M it is again of size 2. Second, the criterion degrades with redundancy: by the final checkpoint at 410M and 1B no single head clears the necessity threshold (K→0K\to 0; ablating any one head leaves accuracy at 0.950.95 against a 0.950.95 baseline), because the capability has delocalized into interchangeable copies. A redundancy-robust variant — the smallest group whose joint ablation destroys the capability — grows from 1–2 in the small/early models to 3 in the large/late ones, quantifying the redundancy, but it measures the destruction side (a minimum over links, Prop. 7) and therefore does not substitute for the formation-side count. The honest statement is thus sharper than before: ablation-based part counting is valid before delocalization — which is exactly the engine’s stated operating rule — and beyond it the formation-side KK must be carried by formation-time evidence (the clock’s cross-circuit consistency), not by ablation. That the causal precursor (the previous-token head) remains in the necessary set at every scale and checkpoint where the criterion is defined is what the clock actually relies on, and it is measured to hold throughout.

Relatedly, the same sweep measures the AND-gate structure of real circuits directly: removing one identified part collapses the capability to a median 5%5\% of baseline (range 2–42%), whereas removing a randomly chosen non-part head leaves it at 99–102% of baseline. Graceful, proportional degradation — the signature of a partial-credit architecture — is absent; the collapse is what a conjunction predicts, and it is not an artifact of ablation per se, since the control ablations do nothing. The engine’s one systematic failure is itself confirmatory: at late checkpoints, formed circuits delocalize into redundant copies and single-head ablation loses signal — fixing the operating rule (dissect shortly after ignition) and independently evidencing the redundancy physics.

The AND-gate test at scale, on the engine’s own operating rule. Applying that rule turns the test from anecdote into statistics. Sweeping three scales (70M/160M/410M) ×\times five checkpoints (1k–16k steps, i.e. near ignition rather than at the end of training) ×\times seven capabilities gives 120 cells, of which 32 are discriminating — capability present, and at least two individually necessary parts, so that conjunction and partial credit predict different things (K=1K{=}1 cells are excluded a priori: with one part both models predict collapse). Removing one part leaves a median 16.7%16.7\% of the capability; removing a random non-part head leaves 100%100\%. Against each cell’s own partial-credit prediction (1−1/K1-1/K, i.e. 50–83% retained), 32 of 32 cells fall below, sign test p=2.3×10−10p=2.3\times 10^{-10}; the stricter preregistered criterion (≤25%\leq 25\% retained and controls ≥80%\geq 80\%) passes 22 of 32, the remainder landing at 25–48% — still below partial credit, not above it. Part counts span K=2K=2–66 across IOI, subject–verb agreement, greater-than, in-context learning, word-pair recall, counting, and copying. Six of the 32 were recovered by a preregistered secondary read-out: where baseline accuracy saturates at 100% the instrument has no dynamic range, so we score the unthresholded margin (accuracy is the sign of the margin) — a resolution fix of the same kind as measuring probes in fp32, recorded per cell so the two read-outs are never mixed.

The synthesis, and the boundary as a signed prediction. Full frozen constants (continued-training regime): sites decay slope 0.61±0.090.61\pm 0.09; batch exponent −0.329±0.046-0.329\pm 0.046 (R2R^{2} 0.96); drive exponent γ=0.62±0.01\gamma=0.62\pm 0.01 (R2R^{2} 0.999); barrier β=0.23±0.05\beta=0.23\pm 0.05 (Pythia, off-wall); melt thresholds per Fig. 11. Freezing all single-axis terms and predicting three never-run combinations in which all three axes deviate at once: 8.4% and 1.3% error in the bulk; 112% at the near-floor point, the error growing monotonically with floor proximity (error∝(c−c0)−3.2±0.9\mathrm{error}\propto(c-c_{0})^{-3.2\pm 0.9}, R2R^{2} 0.92 over three points, stated as such). By Corollary 1 this is not an unexplained failure but the predicted signature of part dependence where capacity is shared: the factorized law holds where independence holds and couples at the boundary — the standard structure of nucleation kinetics away from versus near a spinodal — and it is a standing falsifiable commitment: any new combination’s factorization error should be set by its floor distance.

10 Why one law survives a complex model: the rate-determining step

A fair objection runs: a language model contains many circuits, coupled far more richly than a bag of KK parts — dataflow chains across layers, fan-in, cooperative and competitive interactions — so why should a single exponential law with a single KK describe any real capability? The answer is not ours to claim. It is the rate-determining step principle of chemical kinetics [44]: a multi-step mechanism, however elaborate, exhibits the rate law of its slowest step, and the complexity of the remaining steps collapses at the bottleneck. One Arrhenius form underwrites thousands of distinct mechanisms for exactly this reason. What is ours is the demonstration, measurement by measurement, that capability formation has such a bottleneck, that the bottleneck is the subset-signal-free joint alignment, and that its dimensionality is observable:

(i) The cheap steps are cheap and happen early. Circuit stages with independent utility — parts that carry their own gradient signal — form first and fast: the mechanism precedes the behavior in 15/15 model–task pairs (§6), and an exact-depth from-scratch ladder ignites strictly in order, depths 1→41\to 4, in 6/6 seeds. (ii) The expensive step is the joint alignment — and this dichotomy is itself a theorem. Where no strict subset carries signal, a single added part multiplies formation time by >>11×\times (the parity family), against 5.8×\times when subset signal exists (the summed family) — the bottleneck’s cost dwarfs the stages’. The staircase/leap theorems give this measured dichotomy its mathematical backbone: subset-signal-at-every-stage targets are SGD-learnable in O⁡(d)O(d) samples (an iff in the mean-field regime), while an ℓ\ell-wise joint step costs Θ~​(dmax⁡(ℓ−1,1))\tilde{\Theta}(d^{\max(\ell-1,1)}) where proven [21, 22] — cheap stages and an expensive bottleneck are not our metaphor but the proven structure of SGD learning on this function class. (iii) Everything upstream of the bottleneck is kinetically invisible. This is the direct rate-determining-step measurement: in the missing-parts grid (EK-5), waiting time depends only on the size of the remaining joint step, not on how much circuit already stands — rows flat to 1.1–1.4 across total KK. (iv) The wait is governed by one barrier, not a chain of comparable ones. The waiting-time shape is exponential (κ→1.2\kappa\to 1.2, EK-1); a sequence of kk comparable activated steps would instead show an Erlang shape κ≈k\kappa\approx k. (v) The bottleneck’s dimensionality is measurable and load-bearing. The engine’s causally-counted KK is what unifies the clock across different circuits (K=2K{=}2 and K=4K{=}4 sharing one β\beta) while the textbook count fails (§9).

Nor do circuit–circuit interactions reopen unbounded complexity: each measured interaction enters as a correction with a measured form, not a new law. Cross-circuit catalysis makes the rate linear in neighbor density (secondary nucleation; R2R^{2} 0.88 on real models in prior work [25]); competition for shared capacity renormalizes constants rather than the form (in a two-skill furnace the loser’s formation time is renormalized ∼\sim20×\times while each skill alone obeys its own law); and the near-wall coupling carries its own scaling, error∝(c−c0)−3.2\mathrm{error}\propto(c-c_{0})^{-3.2} (§9) — the theory meters its own domain of validity.

The epistemic position this leaves us in is, again, not novel; it is the standard position of physical metallurgy [45]. Nobody derives a steel’s TTT diagram from quantum mechanics — steel is far too complex — yet the framework fixes the diagram’s structure, a handful of measured points fix the alloy’s constants, and the result runs industry. Here the structure (floor, clock, shelf life, melt line) transfers across families, the per-family effective β\beta is the material constant, and one cheap anchor — a single attention readout at 0.36% of training — calibrates a family, after which frozen constants predict held-out models to median 5% (§6). The framework would break, and is built to break visibly, if the rate-limiting step showed non-exponential kinetics, if the precursor stopped dating the composition, or if the causal part-count stopped unifying the constants; none of these has happened in any system tested.

11 Negative results and reproducibility

A design lesson worth more than the result it cost us. Synthetic sequence tasks harbour algebraic shortcuts: alternative solutions of much lower part count that agree with the intended target on the training distribution. We have now hit this family three times — a closed-loop collapse in which a fully-driven conjunction degenerates into single-token copying; a look-up-table task solved by periodic orbits; and the summed design’s two-term recurrence documented above, which silently replaced the intended KK-part solution from K=3K{=}3 upward and cost us a per-part barrier number we have withdrawn. The general prescription we now follow, and recommend: for any synthetic target, (i) search for algebraic identities that relate the target at nearby positions, since these generate low-part-count alternative solutions; (ii) build a discriminating probe — evaluation positions where the shortcut and the intended solution disagree — and report both scores, never the aggregate alone; (iii) prefer designs that are provably shortcut-free (our query-parity design isolates each query behind a gap, so consecutive targets are statistically independent and no cross-position identity exists). A task whose intended solution is never verified against its cheapest alternative is not a measurement of that solution.

The complete failure log is part of the evidence. IOI is un-ignitable in every continued-training arm (its barrier exceeds the regime’s power, consistent with its native t∗t^{*}); greater-than is unwithholdable (plain text already exceeds its floor — capabilities split into withholdable and unwithholdable by food scarcity); a global entropy regularizer does not rescue aged substrates (it also suppresses the peaked circuit it should enable); newborn circuits are narrow-band (food at repetition period 128 does not serve a period-64 probe — a trap hit twice, fixed, and itself evidence that young circuits are distance-specific before delocalization); four attempts at a precursor dose–response were all confounded by precursor redundancy (the causal case rests on the switch and the resets instead); pure-temperature release fails without surgery (§8); three execution artifacts were caught by internal audits (a mirror resolving every revision to one commit — detectable because step-0 weights scored as trained; .bin-only checkpoints refused under a torch CVE policy; an ignition-detector edge case), each with detection criteria for reproducers; and one publicly failed frozen prediction (the occupation tax was frozen as saturating and measured as divergent) is retained because a fitted story would not contain it. Every number is recomputable from released per-experiment JSON files and scripts; the EK premise-test suite (§4.4) was likewise designed and its budgets frozen before running.

12 Honest scope

≤\leq1.4B parameters; two families (the only ones with dense public checkpoints); causal constants belong to a continued-training regime whose token flux is far below native pretraining (the from-scratch reproduction removes the pretrained-substrate confound but not the flux gap); capabilities are mechanism-level plus one task-level demonstration — no benchmark-suite prediction yet; switch/shelf/reset arms at n=5n=5, several others at n=2n=2–3; single hardware/framework stack; fp32 is required for probe evaluation only (softmax scores collapse under bf16 underflow) — models trained in low precision are probed in fp32, so the constraint is on the measurement instrument, not on training practice; the diffusion-approximation regime of Step 1 is itself a scope condition (production optimizer stacks deform the SDE); the engine’s count for induction is less crisp than for IOI; direct-KK measurements span K=2K=2–44, and the wide-KK ladder (Remark 4 ff.) is the stated next experiment; β\beta is single-valued only away from the capacity wall; control results are toy-plus-real-Pythia, not production-scale; the alignment-fragility reading (safety training as the top rung — last in, first out [46]) is a corollary of Prop. 7(b) plus literature, not a direct experiment. The mathematical status is exactly as marked, in three grades. Proved: the no-partial-credit structure of the apparatus (Lemma 1); the exponential-in-KK cost for the task class (query-complexity and leap theorems, §2A, with their stated regimes: SQ/CSQ algorithm classes, single-pass training, large ambient dimension — and no such theorem yet exists for transformers themselves); and the occupation theorem for the backward reading (Theorem 1, App. A) — deadline, data-irrecoverability, reset-repair, and loss-silence, its confinement side free of any mixing assumption, at the price of the model’s stated idealizations (positional attention, oracle gating, the C0 feasibility condition), each idealization flagged in the appendix with its empirical counterpart. Conditional: the nucleation-form propositions, exact given Assumptions 1–3; Assumption 1(b) — mixing for transformer SGD on formation timescales — now burdens only the physical reading (temperature, supersaturation, melting), is beyond present mathematics for anyone, and proving it would upgrade that reading to a theorem: an invitation, not a concession. Measured: everything else, preregistered.

13 Related work: the equilibrium picture, and what a rate adds

Equilibrium theories of training structure. Singular learning theory and developmental interpretability characterize training stages as Bayesian free-energy transitions and detect them post hoc via the local learning coefficient [1, 2, 3]; grokking has an equilibrium first-order model [5] and a Kramers-escape model in linear networks [6]. These supply the statics. None yields a formation-rate law, a precursor clock, an aging horizon, or a control schedule — a free energy is not a rate. Predicting emergence. Aoyama et al. [47] predict induction-head arrival from data statistics with a throughput equation; the prediction is real but mechanism-free. Our clock is derived from a barrier law, reads an internal precursor, and its KK-dependence is forced, not fit; and where Lavie et al. [36] argue softmax-attention emergence is intrinsically unpredictable and Baherwani et al. [37] that timing is initialization-random, the prospective clock results are a direct counterexample at the capability class we cover. Emergence phenomenology. Wei et al. [48], Schaeffer et al. [49], Ganguli et al. [13] debate description; Olsson et al. [32], Elhage et al. [50] identify the induction circuit and its phase change; Reddy [51], Singh et al. [52], Hoogland et al. [2] model and detect its development. We add the quantitative ratio law, frozen-constant prospective validation, cross-family transfer, causal steering, and the plasticity connection. Data mixing. Gu et al. [4] document a mixing-ratio threshold and attribute it to capacity allocation; our floor carries the nucleation signatures (intensivity, near-floor divergence, scale trend) in a mechanistic order parameter (Prop. 4); Xie et al. [10], Liu et al. [11], Ye et al. [12] optimize loss, not which capabilities form. Loss of plasticity. The phenomenon and remedies are established [7, 8, 39]; the causes literature is explicitly partial [9]; Lyle et al. [40] conjecture the emergence–plasticity link via effective learning rate. We supply the quantitative form: one rate equation with law, horizon, located mechanism, repair, and the site/drive discriminator (Prop. 5). Resets as a remedy are standard in that literature [7, 39]; what is new here is not the operation but the causal localization of which weights (attention — with MLP and embedding controls discriminated causally), why (commitment, r=0.93r=0.93), and when (the horizon and its scale law). Non-equilibrium SGD. Broken detailed balance and irreversibility are established [30, 31]; Yaida’s fluctuation–dissipation relations are a measurement tool at stationarity [53]; we add the FDT qualification test, its six-knob failed verdict, and the injected-bath prescription. Control baselines. Injected-noise training is itself classical — simulated annealing, gradient noise [54], SGLD — but is framed there as optimization or exploration; none applies a fluctuation–dissipation qualification, none selects which circuit forms, and none demonstrates pinning or selective dissolution — the operations, not the noise, are the contribution. Grokfast [41] accelerates grokking by gradient filtering without selecting circuits; dual-process steering [55] switches mechanisms by discrete forgetting; our schedules are continuous, bidirectional, and derived from the rate equation. Fragility at coarse grain. Layer- and module-level sensitivity to perturbation and quantization is known; the circuit-grain melt points, their cross-scale constancy, and the build/break duality (Prop. 7) are new. Metaphor. A crystallization framing of training has been proposed qualitatively [56]; this program makes it quantitative and falsifiable. Our own prior work develops single-circuit nucleation with measured Langevin structure [25]; this paper is the generalization to the full life cycle and the control layer.

14 Conclusion

Training has had a phase diagram; this paper gives it a TTT diagram. One rate equation — sites ×\times attempts ×\times supersaturation ×\times barrier, minus destruction — derived under stated assumptions and measured factor by factor, carries a capability from its first invisible precursor through ignition, aging, and, if one chooses, controlled dissolution. Emergence is the equation read forward: a floor, a throttle, and a clock that dates arrival to median 5% before the capability exists. Loss of plasticity is the same equation read backward: a tax, a horizon, a located mechanism, a repair — and, in a controlled model, a theorem — the quantitative law a decade of remedies has been missing. Control is the equation completed: install the temperature SGD lacks, and circuits can be accelerated at the nose, pinned in the glass, released on command, and dissolved selectively at their melt points — scheduled, in short, like the heat treatment of an alloy. The mathematics is exactly as strong as its premises, and the premises are the experiments: joint alignment is a product law (measured), the barrier is additive (measured, with its own deviation theory), the waiting is memoryless (measured), and the one unproved premise — mixing for transformer SGD — is stated as the field’s next theorem to want.

Appendix A The occupation theorem: model, assumptions, and full proofs

This appendix proves Theorem 1. Every step is graded: exact (arithmetic or algebraic identity), in-model theorem (proved under the stated assumptions), cited theorem (an external result with its conditions verified), or explicit assumption. The headline structural fact bears repeating: clauses (ii)–(iv) — the consequences of occupation — use only a drift inequality and bounded increments (Hajek [38]); no ergodicity or mixing enters. Only clause (i), the deadline’s arrival, uses the recruitment assumption (G8), whose empirical counterpart is the measured occupation of §7.
